title.zh: 卷六十一 列傳第二十一 武三王
title.raw: 卷六十一 列傳第二十一 武三王 Volume 61 Biographies 21: Wu Sanwang

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十一 武三王

translations.literal: Biography 21: The Three Princes of Wu
translations.idiomatic: Biography 21: The Three Princes of Wu

sentences.zh: 武帝七男：張夫人生少帝，孫脩華生廬陵孝獻王義真，胡婕妤生文皇帝，王脩容生彭城王義康，袁美人生江夏文獻王義恭，孫美人生南郡王義宣，呂美人生衡陽文王義季。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu had seven sons: Lady Zhang bore Shaodi; Sun Xiuhua bore Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen; Lady Hu the Jieyu bore Emperor Wen; Lady Wang Xiurong bore Prince of Pengcheng Yikang; Lady Yuan bore Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia Yigong; Lady Sun bore Prince of Nanjun Yixuan; Lady Lü bore Prince Wen of Hengyang Yiji.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had seven sons. Lady Zhang gave birth to Shaodi; Sun Xiuhua to Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen; the Jieyu Lady Hu to Emperor Wen; Lady Wang Xiurong to Prince Yikang of Pengcheng; Lady Yuan to Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia, Yigong; Lady Sun to Prince Yixuan of Nanjun; and Lady Lü to Prince Wen of Hengyang, Yiji.

sentences.zh: 義康、義宣別有傳。

translations.literal: Yikang and Yixuan have separate biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Yikang and Yixuan are treated in separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 廬陵孝獻王義真，美儀貌，神情秀徹。

translations.literal: Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen, had handsome features and a clear, refined spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaoxian of Luling, Yizhen, was handsome in bearing, with a spirit clear and penetrating.

sentences.zh: 初封桂陽縣公，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: He was first enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyang County with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Duke of Guiyang County, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 年十二，從北征大軍進長安，留守栢谷塢，除員外散騎常侍，不拜。

translations.literal: At age twelve he followed the northern expedition army into Chang'an, remained to guard Baigu Stockade, was appointed Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and did not accept the office.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he marched with the northern expedition to Chang'an, stayed behind to hold Baigu Stockade, was named Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 及關中平定，高祖議欲東還，而諸將行役既久，咸有歸願，止留偏將，不足鎮固人心，乃以義真行都督雍、涼、秦三州之河東、平陽、河北三郡諸軍事、安西將軍、領護西戎校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong was pacified, Gaozu considered returning east, but the generals had been on campaign long and all wished to go home; leaving only subordinate commanders would not suffice to steady hearts. He therefore made Yizhen acting Commander over the military affairs of the Hedong, Pingyang, and Hebei commanderies of Yong, Liang, and Qin provinces, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protecting the Western Rong, and Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: After Guanzhong was pacified, Gaozu planned to return east. The generals had been in the field so long that all yearned for home, and leaving only subordinate commanders would not have been enough to hold the region steady. He therefore appointed Yizhen acting commander of military affairs for the Hedong, Pingyang, and Hebei commanderies within Yong, Liang, and Qin, General Who Pacifies the West, Colonel Protecting the Western Rong, and Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 太尉諮議參軍京兆王脩為長史，委以關中之任。

translations.literal: Wang Xiu of Jingzhao, Consulting Army Aide to the Grand Marshal, was made Chief Clerk and entrusted with the duties in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu of Jingzhao, consulting army aide to the Grand Marshal, was made chief clerk and entrusted with authority over Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 高祖將還，三秦父老詣門流涕訴曰：「殘民不沾王化，於今百年矣。

translations.literal: As Gaozu was about to return, the elders of the Three Qins came to his gate weeping and pleaded, saying, 'The broken people have not received royal transformation for a hundred years now.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was preparing to leave, the elders of the Three Qins came to his gate in tears and said, 'Our ruined people have not known the king's transforming rule for a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 始睹衣冠，方仰聖澤。

translations.literal: We have only now beheld caps and robes and just now look up to the sage's grace.
translations.idiomatic: We have only just seen civilized dress and only now look up to your sacred grace.

sentences.zh: 長安十陵，是公家墳墓，咸陽宮殿數千間，是公家屋宅，舍此欲何之？」

translations.literal: The ten mausoleums of Chang'an are your family's tombs; the thousands of halls of the Xianyang palaces are your family's dwellings—leaving these, where would you go?'
translations.idiomatic: The ten imperial tombs at Chang'an are your family's graves; the thousands of halls of the Xianyang palaces are your family's houses. If you abandon these, where else would you go?'

sentences.zh: 高祖為之愍然，慰譬曰：「受命朝廷，不得擅留。

translations.literal: Gaozu was moved to pity for them and consoled them, saying, 'Having received the mandate from the court, I cannot remain on my own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was deeply moved and comforted them, saying, 'I hold my commission from the court and cannot stay here on my own authority.

sentences.zh: 感諸君戀本之意，今留第二兒，令文武賢才共鎮此境。」

translations.literal: Touched by your longing for your homeland, I now leave my second son, with civil and military worthies together to guard this region.'
translations.idiomatic: Moved by your devotion to this land, I will leave my second son here, with worthy civil and military men to hold this territory together.'

sentences.zh: 臨還，自執義真手以授王脩，令脩執其子孝孫手以授高祖。

translations.literal: On the eve of his departure he himself took Yizhen's hand and gave it to Wang Xiu, and had Xiu take his son Xiaosun's hand and give it to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, he took Yizhen's hand himself and placed it in Wang Xiu's; he then had Xiu take his own son Xiaosun's hand and place it in Gaozu's.

sentences.zh: 義真尋除正，加節，又進督並東秦二州、司州之東安定、新平二郡諸軍事，領東秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Yizhen soon received regular appointment, was given the staff of authority, and was further advanced to supervise the military affairs of Bing and Eastern Qin provinces and of the Dong'an and Xinping commanderies of Sizhou, and to hold the post of Governor of Eastern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was soon given regular appointment and the staff of command, and was further made supervisor of military affairs for Bing and Eastern Qin and for the Dong'an and Xinping commanderies of Sizhou, while serving as Governor of Eastern Qin.

sentences.zh: 時隴上流人，多在關中，望因大威，復得歸本。

translations.literal: At that time refugees from upstream Longyou were mostly in Guanzhong, hoping through the great prestige to return to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many people from upstream Longyou who had fled were living in Guanzhong, hoping that the dynasty's great prestige would let them return home.

sentences.zh: 及置東秦州，父老知無復經略隴右、固關中之意，咸共歎息。

translations.literal: When Eastern Qin Province was established, the elders knew there was no longer any intent to plan for Longyou or to hold Guanzhong firm, and all sighed together.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Qin Province was set up, the local elders understood that there would be no further effort to recover Longyou or to hold Guanzhong, and they all sighed as one.

sentences.zh: 而佛佛虜寇逼交至。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Fofo barbarians' raids pressed in one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile raids by the Fofo barbarians came in relentless succession.

sentences.zh: 沈田子既殺王鎮惡，王脩又殺田子。

translations.literal: Shen Tianzi had already killed Wang Zhen'e; Wang Xiu then killed Tianzi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tianzi had already killed Wang Zhen'e, and Wang Xiu then killed Tianzi in turn.

sentences.zh: 義真年少，賜與左右不節，脩常裁減之，左右並怨。

translations.literal: Yizhen was young and gave to his attendants without restraint; Xiu often cut back the gifts, and the attendants all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was still young and lavished gifts on his attendants without limit. Xiu often reduced what was granted, and the attendants all bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 因是白義真曰：「鎮惡欲反，故田子殺之。

translations.literal: They therefore reported to Yizhen, saying, 'Zhen'e intended to rebel, so Tianzi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore told Yizhen, 'Zhen'e was plotting rebellion, which is why Tianzi killed him.

sentences.zh: 脩今殺田子，是又欲反也。」

translations.literal: Xiu has now killed Tianzi—this means he too intends to rebel.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiu has now killed Tianzi, which means he too is plotting rebellion.'

sentences.zh: 義真乃使左右劉乞等殺脩。

translations.literal: Yizhen then had his attendants Liu Qi and others kill Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen then had his attendants Liu Qi and others put Xiu to death.

sentences.zh: 脩字叔治，京兆灞城人也。

translations.literal: Xiu, courtesy name Shuzhi, was a man of Bàcheng in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, whose courtesy name was Shuzhi, was from Bàcheng in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 初南渡見桓玄，玄知之，謂曰：「君平世吏部郎才。」

translations.literal: When he first crossed south he met Huan Xuan; Xuan recognized his talent and said, 'Sir, in a peaceful age you would have the talent of a Director of the Ministry of Personnel.'
translations.idiomatic: When he first crossed south to the Yangzi he met Huan Xuan, who recognized his ability and said, 'In a peaceful age you would have the makings of a Director of the Ministry of Personnel.'

sentences.zh: 脩既死，人情離駭，無相統一。

translations.literal: After Xiu died, hearts were scattered in alarm and there was no unified leadership.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu's death morale collapsed in alarm, and no one could hold command together.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣將軍朱齡石替義真鎮關中，使義真輕兵疾歸。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent the general Zhu Lingshi to replace Yizhen in guarding Guanzhong and ordered Yizhen to return east with a light force at speed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent General Zhu Lingshi to relieve Yizhen in Guanzhong and ordered Yizhen to hurry east with a light force.

sentences.zh: 諸將競斂財貨，多載子女，方軌徐行，虜追騎且至。

translations.literal: The generals vied to gather wealth and loaded many women and children; they marched in parallel ranks at an easy pace while the barbarians' pursuing horsemen were about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The generals scrambled to seize goods and loaded their trains with wives and children. They marched in wide ranks at a leisurely pace while the enemy's horsemen were closing in.

sentences.zh: 建威將軍傅弘之曰：「公處分亟進，恐虜追擊人也。

translations.literal: Fu Hongzhi, General Who Establishes Might, said, 'Your orders were to advance swiftly, for fear the barbarians would pursue and strike the men.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Establishes Might Fu Hongzhi said, 'Your orders were to press on quickly, for fear the barbarians would overtake and slaughter the men.

sentences.zh: 今多將輜重，一日行不過十里；

translations.literal: Now with so much baggage train, in one day you advance no more than ten li;
translations.idiomatic: Now you are dragging so much baggage that you cover no more than ten li in a day;

sentences.zh: 虜騎追至，何以待之？

translations.literal: when the barbarian horsemen catch up, how will you face them?
translations.idiomatic: when the barbarian cavalry catches up, how will you answer them?

sentences.zh: 宜棄車輕行，乃可以免。」

translations.literal: You should abandon the carts and travel light—only then can you escape.'
translations.idiomatic: You should abandon the carts and travel light; only then can you get away.'

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: They did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: They would not listen.

sentences.zh: 賊追兵果至，騎數萬匹。

translations.literal: The enemy pursuers did arrive—tens of thousands of horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers came as he had warned: tens of thousands of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍蒯恩斷後，不能禁；

translations.literal: Kuai En, General Who Assists the State, held the rear but could not stop them;
translations.idiomatic: General Who Assists the State Kuai En held the rear but could not hold them back;

sentences.zh: 至青泥，後軍大敗，諸將及府功曹王賜悉被俘虜。

translations.literal: at Qingni the rear army was utterly defeated, and the generals together with the headquarters aide Wang Ci were all taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: at Qingni the rear guard was shattered. The generals and the headquarters aide Wang Ci were all taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 義真在前，故得與數百人奔散。

translations.literal: Yizhen was in the van and so was able to flee scattered with several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen had been in the van and so escaped with a few hundred men in scattered flight.

sentences.zh: 日暮，虜不復窮追。

translations.literal: At dusk the barbarians did not press the pursuit further.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the barbarians gave up the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 義真與左右相失，獨逃草中。

translations.literal: Yizhen became separated from his attendants and fled alone into the grass.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was separated from his attendants and hid alone in the grass.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍段宏單騎追尋，緣道叫喚，義真識其聲，出就之，曰：「君非段中兵邪？

translations.literal: Duan Hong, Central Army Aide, rode alone in search along the road calling out; Yizhen recognized his voice, came out to him, and said, 'Are you not Central Army Aide Duan?
translations.idiomatic: Central Army Aide Duan Hong rode alone along the road calling for him. Yizhen recognized his voice, came out, and said, 'Are you not Central Army Aide Duan?

sentences.zh: 身在此。」

translations.literal: I am here.'
translations.idiomatic: I am here.'

sentences.zh: 宏大喜，負之而歸。

translations.literal: Hong was greatly pleased, carried him on his back, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was overjoyed, lifted him onto his back, and carried him back.

sentences.zh: 義真謂宏曰：「今日之事，誠無算略。

translations.literal: Yizhen said to Hong, 'Today's affair truly lacked any plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen said to Hong, 'What happened today was truly without plan or foresight.

sentences.zh: 然丈夫不經此，何以知艱難。」

translations.literal: Yet if a man does not pass through this, how can he know hardship?'
translations.idiomatic: Yet how is a man to know hardship if he never passes through such a thing?'

sentences.zh: 初，高祖聞青泥敗，未得義真審問，有前至者訪之，並云「暗夜奔敗，無以知存亡」。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu heard of the defeat at Qingni he had not yet received definite word on Yizhen; those who arrived first were questioned, and all said, 'In the dark night we fled in defeat and could not know whether he lived or died.'
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first heard of the defeat at Qingni he had no firm news of Yizhen. He questioned those who arrived ahead, and all said, 'We fled in the dark of night and could not tell whether he lived or died.'

sentences.zh: 高祖怒甚，克日北伐，謝晦諫不從。

translations.literal: Gaozu was furious and set a day for a northern campaign; Xie Hui remonstrated but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was furious and fixed a day for a northern campaign. Xie Hui remonstrated, but he would not be moved.

sentences.zh: 及得宏啟事，知義真已免，乃止。

translations.literal: When he received Hong's report and learned that Yizhen had escaped, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong's report arrived and he learned that Yizhen was safe, he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 義真尋都督司、雍、秦、并、涼五州諸軍、建威將軍、司州刺史，持節如故。

translations.literal: Yizhen soon became Commander over the armies of the five provinces Si, Yong, Qin, Bing, and Liang, General Who Establishes Might, and Governor of Si, holding the staff of authority as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was soon made commander of the armies of Si, Yong, Qin, Bing, and Liang, General Who Establishes Might, and Governor of Si, with the staff of command as before.

sentences.zh: 以段宏為義真諮議參軍，尋遷宋臺黃門郎，領太子右衛率。

translations.literal: Duan Hong was made Yizhen's Consulting Army Aide; he was soon transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate of the Song headquarters and concurrently Commandant of the Crown Prince's Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hong was made Yizhen's consulting army aide, then was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate of the Song headquarters and concurrently served as commandant of the crown prince's right guard.

sentences.zh: 宏，鮮卑人也，為慕容超尚書左僕射、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Hong was a Xianbei; he had been Murong Chao's Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was a Xianbei who had served Murong Chao as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖伐廣固，歸降。

translations.literal: When Gaozu attacked Guanggu he surrendered and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu attacked Guanggu he submitted in surrender.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉中，為征虜將軍、青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era of Emperor Wen he served as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen in the Yuanjia era he served as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Governor of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 追贈左將軍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 時義真將鎮洛陽，而河南蕭條，未及修理，改除揚州刺史，鎮石頭。

translations.literal: At that time Yizhen was to garrison Luoyang, but Henan was desolate and had not yet been restored; his appointment was changed to Governor of Yangzhou, garrisoning Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was then to garrison Luoyang, but Henan was still wasted and unrestored, so he was reassigned as Governor of Yangzhou and posted at Shitou.

sentences.zh: 義真聰明愛文義，而輕動無德業。

translations.literal: Yizhen was clever and loved literary culture, but was impulsive and without solid virtue or achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was clever and loved letters, but he was impulsive and lacked solid virtue or achievement.

sentences.zh: 與陳郡謝靈運、琅邪顏延之、慧琳道人並周旋異常，云得志之日，以靈運、延之為宰相，慧琳為西豫州都督。

translations.literal: With Xie Lingyun of Chen commandery, Yan Yanzhi of Langye, and the monk Huilin he kept extraordinary company, saying that when he achieved his ambition he would make Lingyun and Yanzhi his chief ministers and Huilin Commander of Western Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He kept unusually close company with Xie Lingyun of Chen, Yan Yanzhi of Langye, and the monk Huilin, saying that when his day came he would make Lingyun and Yanzhi his chief ministers and Huilin commander of Western Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 徐羨之等嫌義真與靈運、延之昵狎過甚，故使范晏從容戒之。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi and the others resented that Yizhen was too intimate with Lingyun and Yanzhi, and so had Fan Yan gently admonish him.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi and his colleagues disliked how familiar Yizhen had become with Lingyun and Yanzhi, and had Fan Yan gently warn him.

sentences.zh: 義真曰：「靈運空疏，延之隘薄，魏文帝云鮮能以名節自立者。

translations.literal: Yizhen said, 'Lingyun is empty and loose, Yanzhi narrow and shallow—as Emperor Wen of Wei said, few can stand on reputation and integrity by themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen replied, 'Lingyun is hollow and undisciplined, Yanzhi cramped and petty. As Emperor Wen of Wei said, few men can stand on reputation and integrity alone.

sentences.zh: 但性情所得，未能忘言於悟賞，故與之遊耳。」

translations.literal: But in what temperament affords I cannot forget words in shared insight and appreciation, and so I keep company with them.'
translations.idiomatic: But temperament draws me to them, and I cannot give up talk in shared insight and delight, so I keep their company—that is all.'

sentences.zh: 將之鎮，列部伍於東府前，既有國哀，義真所乘舫單素，不及母孫脩儀所乘者。

translations.literal: When he was about to go to his post he drew up his troops before the Eastern Palace; as there was national mourning, the barge Yizhen rode was plain and simple and did not match that of his mother, Lady Sun Xiuyi.
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving for his post he drew up his troops before the Eastern Palace. With the court in mourning, the barge Yizhen took was plain and could not compare with that of his mother, Lady Sun Xiuyi.

sentences.zh: 義真與靈運、延之、慧琳等共視部伍，因宴舫內，使左右剔母舫函道以施己舫，而取其勝者。

translations.literal: Yizhen with Lingyun, Yanzhi, Huilin, and the rest together reviewed the troops and then feasted inside the barge; he had his attendants strip the covered passage from his mother's barge to fit his own and took the finer fittings.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen reviewed the troops with Lingyun, Yanzhi, Huilin, and the others, then feasted aboard his barge. He had his men strip the covered passage from his mother's vessel to fit his own and took whatever was finer.

sentences.zh: 及至歷陽，多所求索；

translations.literal: When he reached Liyang he made many demands;
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Liyang he made many demands;

sentences.zh: 羨之等每裁量不盡與，深怨執政，表求還都。

translations.literal: Xu Xianzhi and the others each time trimmed what was granted and did not give all he asked; he deeply resented those in power and memorialized asking to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xianzhi and his colleagues each time granted less than he asked, which deepened his resentment of the government. He memorialized asking to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 而少帝失德，羨之等密謀廢立，則次第應在義真，以義真輕訬，不任主社稷，因其與少帝不協，乃奏廢之，曰：

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shaodi was without virtue; Xu Xianzhi and the others secretly plotted deposition and succession, and by order Yizhen should have been next—yet because Yizhen was frivolous and disrespectful and unfit to hold the altars of state, and because he was at odds with Shaodi, they memorialized to depose him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Shaodi meanwhile was without virtue. Xu Xianzhi and his colleagues secretly plotted deposition and succession; by order Yizhen should have been next, but because he was frivolous, disrespectful, and unfit to hold the altars of state, and because he was at odds with Shaodi, they memorialized for his deposition, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞二叔不咸，難結隆周，淮南悖縱，禍興盛漢，莫不義以斷恩，情為法屈。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when the Two Uncles were not harmonious it was hard to build lofty Zhou, and when Huainan was rebellious and unrestrained disaster rose in flourishing Han—all alike broke kinship by righteousness and bent affection to law.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that when the Two Uncles were not at peace, lofty Zhou could hardly be secured, and when Huainan was rebellious and unrestrained, disaster arose in flourishing Han. In every case righteousness cut through kinship and private feeling yielded to law.

sentences.zh: 二代之事，殷鑒無遠，仁厚之主，行之不疑。

translations.literal: Matters of the two dynasties are mirrors not far off; benevolent and generous rulers carry such measures out without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of those two dynasties are a mirror close at hand, and benevolent rulers have acted on them without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 故共叔不斷，幾傾鄭國；

translations.literal: Thus when Duke Gongshu was not cut off he nearly overturned the state of Zheng;
translations.idiomatic: When Duke Gongshu was not removed, he nearly overturned the state of Zheng;

sentences.zh: 劉英容養，釁廣難深。

translations.literal: when Liu Ying was indulgently nurtured, the omen spread and the trouble ran deep.
translations.idiomatic: when Liu Ying was indulgently kept alive, the omen spread and the trouble ran deep.

sentences.zh: 前事之不忘，後王之成鑒也。

translations.literal: Not forgetting what went before is how later kings complete their mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: Not to forget what went before is how later kings learn their lesson.

sentences.zh: 案車騎將軍義真，凶忍之性，爰自稚弱，咸陽之酷，醜聲遠播。

translations.literal: We find that Yizhen, General of the Chariots and Cavalry, has a fierce and cruel nature from childhood; the atrocities at Xianyang spread his ugly reputation far.
translations.idiomatic: We find that Yizhen, General of the Chariots and Cavalry, has been fierce and cruel from childhood, and the atrocities at Xianyang spread his ugly fame far and wide.

sentences.zh: 先朝猶以年在紈綺，冀能改厲，天屬之愛，想聞革心。

translations.literal: The previous court still considered that in the silk of youth he might reform and grow stern; the love of a kinsman by Heaven's line hoped to hear that his heart had changed.
translations.idiomatic: The previous court still thought that in the silk of youth he might reform, and kinship's love hoped to hear that his heart had turned.

sentences.zh: 自聖體不豫，以及大漸，臣庶憂惶，內外屏氣。

translations.literal: From the time the sacred person was unwell until the final decline, ministers and commoners were anxious in fear, inside and outside holding their breath.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the late emperor fell ill until his final decline, officials and people alike were anxious, and throughout the court men held their breath.

sentences.zh: 而縱博酣酒，日夜無輟，肆口縱言，多行無禮。

translations.literal: Yet he gave himself to gambling and heavy drinking without cease day or night, spoke recklessly with an unbridled mouth, and often acted without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he gave himself to gambling and heavy drinking without cease, spoke recklessly, and often behaved without propriety.

sentences.zh: 先帝貽厥之謀，圖慮經固，親敕陛下，面詔臣等，若遂不悛，必加放黜；

translations.literal: The late emperor's plan left to posterity was plotted with enduring foresight; he personally charged Your Majesty and face to face instructed us your servants that if he still would not repent he must be dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's plan for posterity was laid with enduring foresight. He charged Your Majesty in person and instructed us face to face that if Yizhen still would not repent, he must be removed;

sentences.zh: 至言苦厲，猶在紙翰。

translations.literal: those stern and bitter words still remain on paper.
translations.idiomatic: those stern words still stand written on paper.

sentences.zh: 而自茲迄今，日月增甚，至乃委棄藩屏，志還京邑，潛懷異圖，希幸非冀，轉聚甲卒，徵召車馬。

translations.literal: Yet from then until now the days and months have grown worse, to the point of abandoning his frontier post, his heart set on returning to the capital, secretly harboring other designs and hoping for improper fortune, gathering armor and troops and summoning chariots and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from then until now his conduct has grown worse by the day. He has abandoned his frontier post, set his heart on returning to the capital, secretly harbored other designs, and gathered troops and chariots.

sentences.zh: 陵墳未乾，情事猶昨，遂蔑棄遺旨，顯違成規，整棹浮舟，以示歸志，肆心專己，無復諮承。

translations.literal: The imperial tombs are not yet dry and the affair is still as of yesterday, yet he has scorned the testamentary charge, openly violated established rules, fitted oars and launched boats to show his intent to return, and indulged his own will without further consultation.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor's tomb is not yet dry and these matters are still as fresh as yesterday, yet he has scorned the testament, openly broken established rules, fitted out boats to show his intent to return, and indulged his own will without consulting anyone.

sentences.zh: 聖恩低徊，深垂隱忍，屢遣中使，苦相敦釋。

translations.literal: Your sacred grace has lingered in hesitation and deeply shown forbearance, repeatedly sending palace envoys to earnestly urge release from his course.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's grace has lingered long in forbearance, and palace envoys have been sent again and again to urge him to relent.

sentences.zh: 而親對散騎侍郎邢安泰、廣武將軍茅仲思，縱其悖罵，訕主謗朝，此久播於遠近，暴於人聽。

translations.literal: Yet in person before Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Xing Antai and General of Broad Might Mao Zhongsi he allowed their insolent cursing, mocking the ruler and slandering the court—this has long been broadcast near and far and exposed to all who hear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet before Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Xing Antai and General of Broad Might Mao Zhongsi he allowed their insolent abuse, mocking the ruler and slandering the court—conduct long known near and far and exposed to all.

sentences.zh: 臣聞原火不撲，蔓草難除；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that if a spark in the field is not stamped out, creeping weeds are hard to uproot;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that if a spark in the field is not stamped out, creeping weeds are hard to uproot;

sentences.zh: 青青不伐，終致尋斧。

translations.literal: if the green is not cut down, in the end one must take up the hatchet.
translations.idiomatic: if the green growth is not cut down, in the end one must take up the hatchet.

sentences.zh: 況憂深患著，社稷慮切。

translations.literal: How much more when worry runs deep, harm is manifest, and concern for the altars of state is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when worry runs deep, harm is plain, and concern for the altars of state is urgent.

sentences.zh: 請一遵晉朝武陵舊典，使顧懷之旨，不墜於武廟；

translations.literal: We ask to follow once the old precedent of Wuling in the Jin dynasty, so that the intent of looking back with care may not fall from the Martial Temple;
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the old precedent of Prince Wuling of Jin be followed once, so that the intent of familial regard may not be lost from the ancestral temple;

sentences.zh: 全宥之德，獲申於昵親。

translations.literal: and the virtue of full pardon may be expressed toward a close kinsman.
translations.idiomatic: and the virtue of full pardon may still be shown toward a close kinsman.

sentences.zh: 仰尋感慟，臨啟悲咽。

translations.literal: Looking up in remembrance we are moved to grief; as we present this memorial we choke with sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: As we recall these matters we are moved to grief; presenting this memorial we choke with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 乃廢義真為庶人，徙新安郡。

translations.literal: Yizhen was then deposed as a commoner and moved to Xin'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was then deposed to commoner status and exiled to Xin'an commandery.

sentences.zh: 前吉陽令堂邑張約之上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhang Yuezhi of Tangyi, former magistrate of Jiyang, submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuezhi of Tangyi, former magistrate of Jiyang, submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞仁義之在天下，若中原之有菽；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that benevolence and righteousness in the realm are like beans in the central plains;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that benevolence and righteousness in the realm are like beans in the central plains—

sentences.zh: 理感之被萬物，故不繋於貴賤。

translations.literal: principle and feeling reach all things and therefore are not tied to noble or base.
translations.idiomatic: principle and feeling reach all things and are not bound to noble or base rank.

sentences.zh: 是以考叔反悔誓於及泉，壺關復冤魂於湖邑。

translations.literal: Thus Kaoshu turned back his oath at the Yellow Spring, and Huguan restored a wronged soul at Huyi.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Kaoshu revoked his oath at the Yellow Spring, and the magistrate of Huguan restored a wronged soul at Huyi.

sentences.zh: 當斯之時，豈無尊卿賢輔，或以事迫心違，或以道壅謀屈，何嘗不願聞善於輿隸，藥石於阿氏哉！

translations.literal: At such times were there not honored ministers and worthy aides who, whether because affairs pressed and hearts opposed, or because the Way was blocked and plans bent, never wished to hear good counsel from chariot attendants or take medicine-stone from a nurse?
translations.idiomatic: At such times were there not honored ministers and worthy aides who, whether pressed by events or blocked in counsel, still wished to hear good advice even from a chariot groom or take harsh medicine even from a nurse?

sentences.zh: 臣雖草芥，備充黔首，少不量力，頗高殉義之風，謂蹈善於朝聞，愈徒生於白首。

translations.literal: Your servant, though mere grass, stands among the black-haired people; young and not measuring my strength, I hold high the wind of dying for righteousness, thinking it better to practice good on hearing it at dawn than to live uselessly to white hair.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, though no more than grass among the people, does not measure his strength and holds high the spirit of dying for righteousness, believing it better to do good the moment one hears of it than to live uselessly to white hair.

sentences.zh: 用敢干禁忘戮，披敘丹愚。

translations.literal: Therefore I dare transgress prohibition and forget punishment, and lay bare my loyal foolishness.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I dare transgress prohibition and forget punishment, and lay bare my loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 伏惟高祖武皇帝誕茲神武，撫運龍興，仰清天步，則齊德有虞，俯廓九州，則侔功大夏，故虔順天人，享有萬國。

translations.literal: I bow before Gaozu the Martial Emperor, who brought forth this divine martial power, grasped the turning fortune as the dragon rose, looking up cleared the heavenly steps to match the virtue of Yu of Shun, looking down swept the Nine Regions to rival the achievement of the Great Xia—therefore reverently following Heaven and man he possessed the ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: I bow before Gaozu the Martial Emperor, who brought forth divine martial power and seized the turning fortune as the dragon rose. Looking up he cleared the heavenly steps to match the virtue of Shun's Yu; looking down he swept the Nine Regions to rival the achievement of the Great Xia. Reverently following Heaven and man, he held the realm.

sentences.zh: 雖靈祚修長，聖躬弗永，陛下繼明紹統，遐邇一心，藩王哲茂，四維寧謐，傾耳康哉之詠，企踵升平之風。

translations.literal: Though the sacred mandate was long, the sacred person was not enduring; Your Majesty has succeeded to the bright inheritance, near and far are of one heart, the feudal princes are wise and flourishing, the four bonds are tranquil, all incline the ear to songs of peace and set heel toward the wind of rising tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: Though the sacred mandate was long, the late emperor's life was not. Your Majesty has succeeded to the bright inheritance; near and far are united, the feudal princes flourish in wisdom, the four bonds are at peace, and all incline the ear to songs of peace and set their hopes on rising tranquility.

sentences.zh: 竊念廬陵王少蒙先皇優慈之遇，長受陛下睦愛之恩。

translations.literal: I reflect that the Prince of Luling in youth received the late emperor's gracious favor and in maturity has long received Your Majesty's loving kindness.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the Prince of Luling in youth received the late emperor's gracious favor and has long enjoyed Your Majesty's loving kindness.

sentences.zh: 故在心必言，所懷必亮，容犯臣子之道，致招驕恣之愆。

translations.literal: Therefore what was in his heart he spoke, what he harbored he showed openly; he may have transgressed the way of subject and son and brought on the fault of arrogance and license.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he spoke what was in his heart and showed what he harbored openly. He may have transgressed the way of a subject and son and brought on the fault of arrogance and license.

sentences.zh: 至於天姿夙成，實有卓然之美。

translations.literal: As for his Heaven-given nature formed early, he truly has outstanding beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his Heaven-given gifts matured early, and he truly has outstanding qualities.

sentences.zh: 宜在容養，錄善掩瑕，訓盡義方，進退以漸。

translations.literal: He should be nurtured with tolerance, his good recorded and flaws covered, instructed fully in righteous conduct, advanced and withdrawn by gradual steps.
translations.idiomatic: He should be nurtured with tolerance, his good noted and his flaws covered, instructed fully in righteous conduct, and advanced or restrained by gradual steps.

sentences.zh: 今猥加剝辱，幽徙遠郡，上傷陛下棠棣之篤，下令遠近恇然失圖，士庶杜口，人為身計。

translations.literal: Now to add stripping and humiliation and exile him in a distant commandery wounds Your Majesty's deep fraternal feeling, makes near and far lose their bearings in alarm, seals the mouths of scholars and commoners, and sets each man to planning for himself alone.
translations.idiomatic: Now to strip and humiliate him and exile him to a distant commandery wounds Your Majesty's deep brotherly bond, throws near and far into alarm and confusion, seals the mouths of scholars and commoners, and sets every man to planning only for himself.

sentences.zh: 臣伏思大宋之興，雖協應符緯，而開基造次，根條未繁。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that though the rise of Great Song accorded with omens and registers, the founding was hurried and the roots and branches are not yet luxuriant.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that though the rise of Great Song accorded with omens and registers, the foundation was laid in haste and its roots are not yet deep.

sentences.zh: 宜廣樹藩戚，敦睦以道，使兄弟之美，比輝魯、衛；

translations.literal: It is fitting to plant feudal kin widely and foster brotherhood by the Way, so that the beauty of fraternal harmony may shine like Lu and Wei;
translations.idiomatic: The court should plant feudal kin widely and foster brotherhood by the Way, so that brotherly harmony may shine like Lu and Wei;

sentences.zh: 龜策告同，祚均七百，豈不善哉！

translations.literal: when tortoise and milfoil alike proclaim unity, the fortune may match seven hundred years—would that not be excellent!
translations.idiomatic: when tortoise and milfoil alike proclaim unity, the fortune may match seven hundred years—would that not be excellent!

sentences.zh: 陛下富於春秋，慮未重複，忽安危之遠算，肆不忍於一朝。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is rich in youth and your deliberations are not yet fully formed; you have suddenly set aside far-reaching calculations of safety and danger and indulged unwillingness for a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is still young and your deliberations are not yet fully formed; you have set aside far-reaching calculations of safety and danger and indulged pity for a single morning.

sentences.zh: 特願留神允思，重加詢采。

translations.literal: I earnestly hope you will keep your mind open and grant further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly hope you will keep your mind open and grant further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 上考前代興亡之由，中存武皇締構之業，下顧蒼生顒顒之望，時開曲宥，反王都邑。

translations.literal: Look up to examine the causes of rise and fall in former ages, hold fast in the middle to the Martial Emperor's work of founding, look down to the people's eager hopes, open merciful pardon in season, and return the prince to his capital fief.
translations.idiomatic: Look up to the causes of rise and fall in former ages, hold fast to the Martial Emperor's work of founding, look down to the people's eager hopes, open merciful pardon in season, and return the prince to his capital fief.

sentences.zh: 選保傅於舊老，求四友於髦俊，引誘情性，導達聰明。

translations.literal: Choose tutors from among the old and loyal, seek four companions among outstanding youths, guide his nature, and lead his intelligence to clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Choose tutors from among the old and loyal, seek four companions among outstanding youths, guide his nature, and lead his intelligence to clarity.

sentences.zh: 凡人在苦，皆能自厲，況王質朗心聰，易加訓範。

translations.literal: All men in hardship can discipline themselves—how much more one whose princely substance is bright and whose heart is keen, and who is easy to instruct and mold.
translations.idiomatic: All men in hardship can discipline themselves—how much more one whose princely substance is bright and whose heart is keen, and who may easily be instructed and molded.

sentences.zh: 且中賢之人，未能無過；

translations.literal: Moreover, men of middling talent cannot be without fault;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, men of middling talent cannot be without fault;

sentences.zh: 過貴自改，罪願自新。

translations.literal: when fault is costly they reform themselves; when guilt is heavy they wish to renew themselves.
translations.idiomatic: when fault weighs heavily they reform themselves; when guilt is heavy they wish to make themselves new.

sentences.zh: 以武皇之愛子，陛下之懿弟，豈可以其一眚，長致淪棄哉！

translations.literal: As the Martial Emperor's beloved son and Your Majesty's worthy younger brother, how can one fault long consign him to ruin!
translations.idiomatic: As the Martial Emperor's beloved son and Your Majesty's worthy younger brother, how can one fault long consign him to ruin!

sentences.zh: 謹昧死詣闕，伏地以聞。

translations.literal: I venture to risk death and come to the palace gate, prostrate on the ground to report.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to risk death and come to the palace gate, prostrate on the ground to report.

sentences.zh: 惟願丹誠，一經天聽，退就斧钁，無愧地下矣。

translations.literal: I only pray that my loyal heart may once reach Heaven's hearing; then I may go beneath the axe without shame before the dead.
translations.idiomatic: I only pray that my loyal heart may once reach Heaven's hearing; then I may go beneath the axe without shame before the dead.

sentences.zh: 書奏，以約之為梁州府參軍，尋又見殺。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Yuezhi was made Army Aide of Liangzhou headquarters; soon afterward he too was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Yuezhi was made army aide of the Liangzhou headquarters; soon afterward he too was killed.

sentences.zh: 景平二年六月癸未，羨之等遣使殺義真於徙所，時年十八。

translations.literal: On the guimwei day of the sixth month of the second year of Jingping, Xu Xianzhi and the others sent agents to kill Yizhen at his place of exile; he was eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimwei day of the sixth month of the second year of Jingping, Xu Xianzhi and his colleagues sent agents to kill Yizhen at his place of exile; he was eighteen.

sentences.zh: 元嘉元年八月，詔曰：「前廬陵王靈柩在遠，國封墮替，感惟拱慟，情若貫割。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanjia an edict said, "The former coffin of the Prince of Luling lies far away, the state fief fallen and broken; moved to grief and anguish, my feelings are as if pierced through.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Yuanjia an edict said, "The former coffin of the Prince of Luling lies far away and his state fief lies in ruin; moved to grief and anguish, my feelings are as if pierced through.

sentences.zh: 王體自至極，地戚屬尊，豈可令情禮永淪，終始無寄。

translations.literal: The prince's person reached the utmost of kinship and his place among earthly relatives was honored—how can feeling and ritual be forever lost, with no resting place from beginning to end?
translations.idiomatic: The prince's person reached the utmost of kinship and his place among earthly relatives was honored—how can feeling and ritual be forever lost, with no resting place from beginning to end?

sentences.zh: 可追復先封，特遣奉迎，並孫脩華、謝妃一時俱還。

translations.literal: His former enfeoffment may be restored and a special envoy sent to welcome him back, together with Sun Xiuhua and Consort Xie all at once.
translations.idiomatic: His former enfeoffment may be restored and a special envoy sent to welcome him back, together with Sun Xiuhua and Consort Xie all at once.

sentences.zh: 言增摧哽。」

translations.literal: Words add to choking grief."
translations.idiomatic: Words add to choking grief."

sentences.zh: 三年正月，誅徐羨之、傅亮等。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and the rest were executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Xu Xianzhi, Fu Liang, and the rest were executed.

sentences.zh: 是日詔曰：「故廬陵王含章履正，英哲自然，道心內昭，徽風遐被。

translations.literal: That day an edict said, "The late Prince of Luling embodied grace and walked in rectitude, naturally wise and brilliant; the Way shone within him and his fine wind spread far.
translations.idiomatic: That day an edict said, "The late Prince of Luling embodied grace and walked in rectitude, naturally wise and brilliant; the Way shone within him and his fine wind spread far.

sentences.zh: 遭時多難，志匡權逼，天未悔禍，運鍾屯險，群凶肆醜，專竊國柄，禍心潛構，釁生不圖。

translations.literal: He met an age of many hardships and wished to set right coerced power, but Heaven did not repent the calamity and fortune turned to peril; the villains committed outrage, usurped the handles of state, harbored treacherous designs in secret, and trouble arose unlooked for.
translations.idiomatic: He met an age of many hardships and wished to set right coerced power, but Heaven did not repent the calamity and fortune turned to peril; the villains committed outrage, usurped the handles of state, harbored treacherous designs in secret, and trouble arose unlooked for.

sentences.zh: 朕每永念讎恥，含痛內結，遵養奸慝，情禮未申。

translations.literal: We ever brood on this shameful wrong and harbor pain within, nurturing the wicked in forbearance while feeling and ritual were not expressed.
translations.idiomatic: We ever brood on this shameful wrong and harbor pain within, nurturing the wicked in forbearance while feeling and ritual were not expressed.

sentences.zh: 今王道既亨，政刑始判，宣昭國體，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Now the royal Way is open and government and punishment begin to be distinguished; to proclaim the body of the state lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: Now the royal Way is open and government and punishment begin to be distinguished; to proclaim the body of the state lies in this.

sentences.zh: 可追崇侍中、大將軍，王如故。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously honored as Palace Attendant and Grand General, with his princely title as before.
translations.idiomatic: He may be posthumously honored as Palace Attendant and Grand General, with his princely title as before.

sentences.zh: 為慰冤魂，少申悲憤。」

translations.literal: To comfort his wronged soul and slightly ease grief and indignation."
translations.idiomatic: To comfort his wronged soul and slightly ease grief and indignation."

sentences.zh: 又詔曰：「乃者權臣陵縱，兆亂基禍，故吉陽令張約之抗疏矢言，至誠慷慨，遂事屈群醜，殞命遐疆，志節不申，感焉兼至。

translations.literal: Another edict said, "Formerly powerful ministers were overbearing and disorder laid the foundation of disaster; therefore Jiyang Magistrate Zhang Yuezhi submitted a forthright memorial with loyal and ardent words, but the affair was crushed by the villains and he lost his life in a distant border; his will and integrity were not fulfilled, and our grief is doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "Formerly powerful ministers were overbearing and disorder laid the foundation of disaster; therefore Jiyang Magistrate Zhang Yuezhi submitted a forthright memorial with loyal and ardent words, but the affair was crushed by the villains and he lost his life in a distant border; his will and integrity were not fulfilled, and our grief is doubled.

sentences.zh: 昔關老奏書，見紀漢策，閻纂獻規，荷榮晉代。

translations.literal: In old times Guan the Elder presented a memorial and was recorded in Han annals; Yan Zuan offered remonstrance and was honored in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In old times Guan the Elder presented a memorial and was recorded in Han annals; Yan Zuan offered remonstrance and was honored in Jin.

sentences.zh: 考其忠概，參跡前蹤，宜加旌顯，式揚義烈。

translations.literal: Examining their loyal integrity, their tracks may be set beside those of old; they should be further honored and displayed, to spread righteous fervor.
translations.idiomatic: Examining their loyal integrity, their tracks may be set beside those of old; they should be further honored and displayed, to spread righteous fervor.

sentences.zh: 可贈以一郡，賜錢十萬，布百匹。」

translations.literal: He may be granted one commandery and given one hundred thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth."
translations.idiomatic: He may be granted one commandery and given one hundred thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth."

sentences.zh: 江夏文獻王義恭，幼而明穎，姿顏美麗，高祖特所鍾愛，諸子莫及也。

translations.literal: Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia, Yigong, was clever and bright from childhood, with a beautiful countenance; Gaozu especially cherished him, and none of the other sons could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia, Yigong, was clever and bright from childhood, with a beautiful countenance; Gaozu especially cherished him, and none of the other sons could compare.

sentences.zh: 飲食寢臥，常不離於側。

translations.literal: In eating, drinking, sleeping, and waking he was never far from his side.
translations.idiomatic: In eating, drinking, sleeping, and waking he was never far from his side.

sentences.zh: 高祖為性儉約，諸子食不過五盞盤，而義恭愛寵異常，求須果食，日中無算，得未嘗啖，悉以乞與傍人。

translations.literal: Gaozu was frugal by nature; the sons' meals were limited to five dishes, yet Yigong was favored beyond measure—he asked for fruits and delicacies without count through the day, and what he received he often did not eat but gave entirely to those beside him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was frugal by nature; the sons' meals were limited to five dishes, yet Yigong was favored beyond measure—he asked for fruits and delicacies without count through the day, and what he received he often did not eat but gave entirely to those beside him.

sentences.zh: 廬陵諸王未嘗敢求，求亦不得。

translations.literal: The princes of Luling never dared to ask; if they asked they did not receive.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of Luling never dared to ask; if they asked they did not receive.

sentences.zh: 汝以弱冠，便親方任。

translations.literal: You at weak crown already hold a frontier post in person.
translations.idiomatic: You at weak crown already hold a frontier post in person.

sentences.zh: 天下艱難，家國事重，雖曰守成，實亦未易。

translations.literal: The realm is hard, state and family affairs weighty; though it is called keeping the inheritance, in truth it is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is hard, state and family affairs weighty; though it is called keeping the inheritance, in truth it is not easy.

sentences.zh: 隆替安危，在吾曹耳，豈可不感尋王業，大懼負荷。

translations.literal: Rise and fall, safety and danger rest in us—how can we fail to reflect on the royal enterprise and greatly fear the burden we bear?
translations.idiomatic: Rise and fall, safety and danger rest in us—how can we fail to reflect on the royal enterprise and greatly fear the burden we bear?

sentences.zh: 今既分張，言集無日，無由復得動相規誨，宜深自砥礪，思而後行。

translations.literal: Now that we are parted, there will be days without gathering; we can no longer move together to admonish each other. You should temper yourself deeply, think before you act.
translations.idiomatic: Now that we are parted, there will be days without gathering; we can no longer move together to admonish each other. You should temper yourself deeply and think before you act.

sentences.zh: 開布誠心，厝懷平當，親禮國士，友接佳流，識別賢愚，鑒察邪正，然後能盡君子之心，收小人之力。

translations.literal: Open your sincere heart, set your breast on fairness, honor the gentlemen of the state, befriend excellent men, distinguish the worthy from the foolish, and examine the straight and the crooked—only then can you exhaust the heart of a gentleman and gather the strength of petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Open your sincere heart, set your breast on fairness, honor the gentlemen of the state, befriend excellent men, distinguish the worthy from the foolish, and examine the straight and the crooked—only then can you exhaust the heart of a gentleman and gather the strength of petty men.

sentences.zh: 汝神意爽悟，有日新之美，而進德修業，未有可稱，吾所以恨之而不能已已者也。

translations.literal: Your spirit is bright and perceptive, with the beauty of daily renewal, yet in advancing virtue and cultivating achievement there is nothing to praise—this is what I regret and cannot cease regretting.
translations.idiomatic: Your spirit is bright and perceptive, with the beauty of daily renewal, yet in advancing virtue and cultivating achievement there is nothing to praise—this is what I regret and cannot cease regretting.

sentences.zh: 汝性褊急，袁太妃亦說如此。

translations.literal: Your nature is narrow and quick; the Grand Imperial Consort Yuan also says the same.
translations.idiomatic: Your nature is narrow and quick; the Grand Imperial Consort Yuan also says the same.

sentences.zh: 性之所滯，其欲必行，意所不在，從物回改，此最弊事。

translations.literal: What nature sticks to, desire must carry out; what the mind does not dwell on, it turns with things—this is the greatest harm.
translations.idiomatic: What nature sticks to, desire must carry out; what the mind does not dwell on, it turns with things—this is the greatest harm.

sentences.zh: 宜應慨然立志，念自裁抑。

translations.literal: You should resolve with emotion to set your will and think of restraining yourself.
translations.idiomatic: You should resolve with emotion to set your will and think of restraining yourself.

sentences.zh: 何至丈夫方欲贊世成名而無斷者哉！

translations.literal: How can a man who wishes to aid the age and make a name be without resolution!
translations.idiomatic: How can a man who wishes to aid the age and make a name be without resolution!

sentences.zh: 今粗疏十數事，汝別時可省也。

translations.literal: Now I roughly set out a dozen matters for you to review when we part.
translations.idiomatic: Now I roughly set out a dozen matters for you to review when we part.

sentences.zh: 遠大者豈可具言，細碎復非筆可盡。

translations.literal: What is far and great cannot be told in full; what is minute and fragmentary cannot be exhausted by the brush.
translations.idiomatic: What is far and great cannot be told in full; what is minute and fragmentary cannot be exhausted by the brush.

sentences.zh: 禮賢下士，聖人垂訓；

translations.literal: To honor the worthy and lower oneself before scholars—the sages left this teaching;
translations.idiomatic: To honor the worthy and lower oneself before scholars—the sages left this teaching;

sentences.zh: 驕侈矜尚，先哲所去。

translations.literal: arrogance, extravagance, and esteem for show—the former sages cast these off.
translations.idiomatic: arrogance, extravagance, and esteem for show—the former sages cast these off.

sentences.zh: 豁達大度，漢祖之德；

translations.literal: Open-mindedness and great tolerance were the virtue of Han's founder;
translations.idiomatic: Open-mindedness and great tolerance were the virtue of Han's founder;

sentences.zh: 猜忌褊急，魏武之累。

translations.literal: suspicion, jealousy, narrowness, and quick temper were the burden of Wei's Martial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: suspicion, jealousy, narrowness, and quick temper were the burden of Wei's Martial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 《漢書》稱衛青云：「大將軍遇士大夫以禮，與小人有恩。」

translations.literal: The Book of Han says of Wei Qing: "The Grand General treated gentlemen with ritual and showed kindness to petty men."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han says of Wei Qing: "The Grand General treated gentlemen with ritual and showed kindness to petty men."

sentences.zh: 西門、安於，矯性齊美；

translations.literal: Ximen Bao and An Yu reformed their natures to equal beauty;
translations.idiomatic: Ximen Bao and An Yu reformed their natures to equal beauty;

sentences.zh: 關羽、張飛，任偏同弊。

translations.literal: Guan Yu and Zhang Fei followed partiality to equal harm.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu and Zhang Fei followed partiality to equal harm.

sentences.zh: 行己舉事，深宜鑒此。

translations.literal: In conduct and in action you should deeply take this as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: In conduct and in action you should deeply take this as a mirror.

sentences.zh: 若事異今日，嗣子幼蒙，司徒便當周公之事，汝不可不盡祗順之理。

translations.literal: If affairs differ from today and the heir is young and tender, the Director of Retainers will then have the affairs of the Duke of Zhou—you must not fail to fulfill the principle of reverent obedience.
translations.idiomatic: If affairs differ from today and the heir is young and tender, the Director of Retainers will then have the affairs of the Duke of Zhou—you must not fail to fulfill the principle of reverent obedience.

sentences.zh: 苟有所懷，密自書陳。

translations.literal: If you harbor any thought, secretly write and report it.
translations.idiomatic: If you harbor any thought, secretly write and report it.

sentences.zh: 若形跡之間，深宜慎護。

translations.literal: In what appears outwardly you should deeply guard yourself.
translations.idiomatic: In what appears outwardly you should deeply guard yourself.

sentences.zh: 至於爾時安危，天下決汝二人耳，勿忘吾言。

translations.literal: When that time comes the safety and danger of the realm will be decided by you two—do not forget my words.
translations.idiomatic: When that time comes the safety and danger of the realm will be decided by you two—do not forget my words.

sentences.zh: 今既進袁太妃供給，計足充諸用，此外一不須復有求取，近亦具白此意。

translations.literal: Now that the Grand Imperial Consort Yuan's provision has been increased, it should suffice for all needs; beyond this you need not ask again—I have recently reported this intention in full.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Grand Imperial Consort Yuan's provision has been increased, it should suffice for all needs; beyond this you need not ask again—I have recently reported this intention in full.

sentences.zh: 唯脫應大餉致，而當時遇有所乏，汝自可少多供奉耳。

translations.literal: Only if a great gift must be sent and at the time something is lacking may you yourself supply a little more or less.
translations.idiomatic: Only if a great gift must be sent and at the time something is lacking may you yourself supply a little more or less.

sentences.zh: 汝一月日自用不可過三十萬，若能省此，益美。

translations.literal: Your personal monthly expenditure should not exceed three hundred thousand; if you can reduce this, so much the better.
translations.idiomatic: Your personal monthly expenditure should not exceed three hundred thousand; if you can reduce this, so much the better.

sentences.zh: 西楚殷曠，常宜早起，接對賓侶，勿使留滯。

translations.literal: Western Chu is broad and empty; you should often rise early, receive and answer guests and companions, and not let them linger.
translations.idiomatic: Western Chu is broad and empty; you should often rise early, receive and answer guests and companions, and not let them linger.

sentences.zh: 判急務訖，然後可入問訊，既睹顏色，審起居，便應即出，不須久停，以廢庶事也。

translations.literal: When urgent business is judged and finished, you may then enter to inquire after us; having seen our countenance and examined how we rise and rest, you should go out at once and not stay long, lest common affairs be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: When urgent business is judged and finished, you may then enter to inquire after us; having seen our countenance and examined how we rise and rest, you should go out at once and not stay long, lest common affairs be neglected.

sentences.zh: 下日及夜，自有餘閑。

translations.literal: Later in the day and at night you will naturally have spare time.
translations.idiomatic: Later in the day and at night you will naturally have spare time.

sentences.zh: 府舍住止，園池堂觀，略所諳究，計當無須改作。

translations.literal: The headquarters residence, gardens, ponds, halls, and towers—I have roughly examined them and reckon they need no rebuilding.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters residence, gardens, ponds, halls, and towers—I have roughly examined them and reckon they need no rebuilding.

sentences.zh: 司徒亦云爾。

translations.literal: The Director of Retainers says the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Retainers says the same.

sentences.zh: 若脫於左右之宜，須小小回易，當以始至一治為限，不煩紛紜，日求新異。

translations.literal: If for the convenience of those about you a small change is needed, it should be limited to one overhaul at first arrival, without daily seeking new alterations.
translations.idiomatic: If for the convenience of those about you a small change is needed, it should be limited to one overhaul at first arrival, without daily seeking new alterations.

sentences.zh: 凡訊獄多決，當時難可逆慮，此實為難，汝復不習，殊當未有次第。

translations.literal: In general criminal interrogations are mostly decided on the spot and are hard to weigh in advance—this is truly difficult, and you are again unpracticed; you will quite lack order.
translations.idiomatic: In general criminal interrogations are mostly decided on the spot and are hard to weigh in advance—this is truly difficult, and you are again unpracticed; you will quite lack order.

sentences.zh: 訊前一二日，取訊簿密與劉湛輩共詳，大不同也。

translations.literal: One or two days before interrogation, take the interrogation register in secret and review it in detail with Liu Zhan and his company—it is greatly different.
translations.idiomatic: One or two days before interrogation, take the interrogation register in secret and review it in detail with Liu Zhan and his company—it is greatly different.

sentences.zh: 至訊日，虛懷博盡，慎無以喜怒加人。

translations.literal: On the day of interrogation, open your heart broadly and exhaust the matter; carefully do not let joy or anger be added to people.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of interrogation, open your heart broadly and exhaust the matter; carefully do not let joy or anger be added to people.

sentences.zh: 能擇善者而從之，美自歸己。

translations.literal: If you can follow the good in others, the beauty returns to yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you can follow the good in others, the beauty returns to yourself.

sentences.zh: 不可專意自決，以矜獨斷之明也。

translations.literal: You must not focus your mind on deciding alone, to boast of the brilliance of solitary judgment.
translations.idiomatic: You must not focus your mind on deciding alone, to boast of the brilliance of solitary judgment.

sentences.zh: 萬一如此，必有大吝，非唯訊獄，君子用心，自不應爾。

translations.literal: If by chance you do so, there will be great regret—not only in interrogation; the heart of a gentleman should not be thus by its own nature.
translations.idiomatic: If by chance you do so, there will be great regret—not only in interrogation; the heart of a gentleman should not be thus by its own nature.

sentences.zh: 刑獄不可壅滯，一月可再訊。

translations.literal: Criminal cases must not be blocked and delayed; once a month you may interrogate again.
translations.idiomatic: Criminal cases must not be blocked and delayed; once a month you may interrogate again.

sentences.zh: 凡事皆應慎密，亦宜豫敕左右，人有至誠，所陳不可漏泄，以負忠信之款也。

translations.literal: All affairs should be kept secret; you should also instruct those about you beforehand that when a man has utmost sincerity, what he presents must not be leaked, lest the pledge of loyal trust be betrayed.
translations.idiomatic: All affairs should be kept secret; you should also instruct those about you beforehand that when a man has utmost sincerity, what he presents must not be leaked, lest the pledge of loyal trust be betrayed.

sentences.zh: 古人言「君不密則失臣，臣不密則失身」。

translations.literal: The ancients said, "If the ruler is not secret he loses his ministers; if the minister is not secret he loses his person."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "If the ruler is not secret he loses his ministers; if the minister is not secret he loses his person."

sentences.zh: 或相讒構，勿輕信受，每有此事，當善察之。

translations.literal: If some slander and plot, do not lightly believe and accept; whenever this occurs, you should examine it well.
translations.idiomatic: If some slander and plot, do not lightly believe and accept; whenever this occurs, you should examine it well.

sentences.zh: 名器深宜慎惜，不可妄以假人。

translations.literal: Titles and vessels should deeply be cherished and not lightly lent to others.
translations.idiomatic: Titles and vessels should deeply be cherished and not lightly lent to others.

sentences.zh: 昵近爵賜，尤應裁量。

translations.literal: Familiar bestowal of ranks and gifts should especially be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Familiar bestowal of ranks and gifts should especially be measured.

sentences.zh: 吾於左右雖為少恩，如聞外論，不以為非也。

translations.literal: Though I am somewhat lacking in kindness to those about me, as I hear from outside opinion, it is not held wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am somewhat lacking in kindness to those about me, as I hear from outside opinion, it is not held wrong.

sentences.zh: 以貴陵物物不服，以威加人人不厭，此易達事耳。

translations.literal: To press down on things with nobility—things do not submit; to add might to men—men are not satisfied; this is easily understood.
translations.idiomatic: To press down on things with nobility—things do not submit; to add might to men—men are not satisfied; this is easily understood.

sentences.zh: 聲樂嬉遊，不宜令過，蒱酒漁獵，一切勿為。

translations.literal: Music, pleasure, and roaming should not be allowed to pass bounds; gambling, wine, fishing, and hunting—do none of these.
translations.idiomatic: Music, pleasure, and roaming should not be allowed to pass bounds; gambling, wine, fishing, and hunting—do none of these.

sentences.zh: 供用奉身，皆有節度；

translations.literal: Provision for the body should all have measure;
translations.idiomatic: Provision for the body should all have measure;

sentences.zh: 奇服異器，不宜興長。

translations.literal: strange dress and curious vessels should not be encouraged to grow.
translations.idiomatic: strange dress and curious vessels should not be encouraged to grow.

sentences.zh: 汝嬪侍左右，已有數人，既始至西，未可匆匆復有所納。

translations.literal: Your consorts and attendants at your side already number several; having just arrived in the west, you must not hastily take more.
translations.idiomatic: Your consorts and attendants at your side already number several; having just arrived in the west, you must not hastily take more.

sentences.zh: 又誡之曰：

translations.literal: He further admonished him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He further admonished him, saying:

sentences.zh: 宜數引見佐史，非唯臣主自應相見。

translations.literal: You should often summon and receive the aides and clerks—not only should lord and subject see each other.
translations.idiomatic: You should often summon and receive the aides and clerks—not only should lord and subject see each other.

sentences.zh: 不數，則彼我不親。

translations.literal: If not often, then he and I will not be close.
translations.idiomatic: If not often, then he and I will not be close.

sentences.zh: 不親則無因得盡人；

translations.literal: If not close, there is no occasion to exhaust men;
translations.idiomatic: If not close, there is no occasion to exhaust men;

sentences.zh: 人不盡，復何由知其眾事。

translations.literal: if men are not exhausted, how can one know their many affairs?
translations.idiomatic: if men are not exhausted, how can one know their many affairs?

sentences.zh: 廣引視聽，既益開博，於言事者，又差有地也。

translations.literal: Broadly drawing in sight and hearing both opens the mind and gives those who speak on affairs a place to stand.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly drawing in sight and hearing both opens the mind and gives those who speak on affairs a place to stand.

sentences.zh: 九年，征為都督南兗、徐、兗、青、冀、幽六州、豫州之梁郡諸軍事、征北將軍、開府儀同三司、南兗州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was recalled as Commander over the military affairs of the six provinces Southern Yan, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You and of Liang commandery in Yuzhou, General Who Campaigns North, Grand Marshal with the Ceremony of the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Southern Yan, garrisoning Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was recalled as commander over the military affairs of Southern Yan, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, and You and of Liang commandery in Yuzhou, General Who Campaigns North, Grand Marshal with the ceremony of the three excellencies, and governor of Southern Yan, garrisoning Guangling.

sentences.zh: 時詔內外百官舉才，義恭上表曰：

translations.literal: At that time an edict ordered civil and military officials inside and outside to recommend talent; Yigong submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict ordered civil and military officials inside and outside to recommend talent; Yigong submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞雲和備樂，則繁會克諧，驊騮驂服，則致遠斯效。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when the cloud-harmony is complete in music, the complex assembly can be tuned; when fine steeds are yoked in the team, distance can be reached.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that when the cloud-harmony is complete in music, the complex assembly can be tuned; when fine steeds are yoked in the team, distance can be reached.

sentences.zh: 陛下順簡夤化，文明在躬，玉衡既正，泰階載一，而猶發慮英髦，垂情仄陋，幽谷空同，顯著揚歷。

translations.literal: Your Majesty follows the turning fortune and transforms by simplicity; civilization is in your person; the jade balance is already correct and the great steps are level as one—yet you still send forth thought for outstanding talent, extend feeling to the narrow and lowly, and make the empty valley and the common hollow alike manifest and rise in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty follows the turning fortune and transforms by simplicity; civilization is in your person; the jade balance is already correct and the great steps are level as one—yet you still send forth thought for outstanding talent, extend feeling to the narrow and lowly, and make the empty valley and the common hollow alike manifest and rise in rank.

sentences.zh: 是以潛虯聳鱗，佇利見之期；

translations.literal: Therefore the hidden dragon raises its scales, awaiting the season of profitable manifestation;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the hidden dragon raises its scales, awaiting the season of profitable manifestation;

sentences.zh: 翔鳳弭翼，應來儀之感。

translations.literal: the soaring phoenix folds its wings, responding to the feeling of coming ritual.
translations.idiomatic: the soaring phoenix folds its wings, responding to the feeling of coming ritual.

sentences.zh: 竊見南陽宗炳，操履閑遠，思業真純，砥節丘園，息賓盛世，貧約而苦，內無改情，軒冕屢招，確爾不拔。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed Zong Bing of Nanyang: his conduct and bearing are serene and far-reaching, his thought and work pure and true; he polishes his integrity in hill and garden and rests from the guest's role in a flourishing age—poor and constrained yet without change within, repeatedly summoned to office and cap yet firmly unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has observed Zong Bing of Nanyang: his conduct and bearing are serene and far-reaching, his thought and work pure and true; he polishes his integrity in hill and garden and rests from the guest's role in a flourishing age—poor and constrained yet without change within, repeatedly summoned to office and cap yet firmly unyielding.

sentences.zh: 若以蒲帛之聘，感以大倫之美，庶投竿釋褐，飜然來儀，必能毗燮九官，宣贊百揆。

translations.literal: If with the gift of plain silk he is moved by the beauty of great human relations, he might cast aside his pole and put on cloth and turn in ritual coming—he would surely be able to assist and harmonize the nine officers and proclaim and support the hundred duties.
translations.idiomatic: If with the gift of plain silk he is moved by the beauty of great human relations, he might cast aside his pole and put on cloth and turn in ritual coming—he would surely be able to assist and harmonize the nine officers and proclaim and support the hundred duties.

sentences.zh: 尚書金部郎臣徐森之，臣府中直兵參軍事臣王天寶，並局力允濟，忠諒款誠。

translations.literal: Your servant, Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue's Gold Bureau Xu Senzhi, and your servant's headquarters Direct Army Aide Wang Tianbao both exert strength in harmony, with loyal sincerity and earnest good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue's Gold Bureau Xu Senzhi, and your servant's headquarters Direct Army Aide Wang Tianbao both exert strength in harmony, with loyal sincerity and earnest good faith.

sentences.zh: 往年逆臣叛逸，華陽失守，森之全境寧民，績章危棘。

translations.literal: In former years rebellious ministers fled and defected; Huayang was lost; Senzhi secured the whole territory and settled the people, his achievements clear amid perilous thorns.
translations.idiomatic: In years past, treacherous ministers rebelled and fled; when Huayang fell, Senzhi secured the entire region and settled the people—his merit stood out amid grave danger.

sentences.zh: 前者經略伊、瀍，元戎喪旅，天寶北勤河朔，東據營丘，勳勇既昭，心事兼竭。

translations.literal: Earlier in campaigning along the Yi and Chan, the commander lost his army; Tianbao toiled north in Heshuo and held Yingqiu in the east—merit and courage were plain, heart and effort both exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When forces campaigned along the Yi and Chan and the chief commander lost his army, Tianbao labored in Heshuo to the north and held Yingqiu in the east; both his valor and his devotion were fully displayed.

sentences.zh: 雖蒙褒敘，未盡才宜，並可授以邊藩，展其志力。

translations.literal: Though they received commendation and promotion, their talents were not fully used; both may be granted frontier posts to display resolve and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Though honored with commendation, their talents have not been fully employed; both should be entrusted with border commands so they may exert their will and strength.

sentences.zh: 交趾遼邈，累喪藩將，政刑每闕，撫蒞惟艱。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi is distant and remote; frontier generals have repeatedly been lost; governance and punishments are often lacking; to govern and rule is especially hard.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi lies far away; the post has repeatedly lost its prefects; administration and justice are often deficient—governing there is uniquely arduous.

sentences.zh: 南中夐遠，風謠迥隔，蠻獠狡竊，邊氓荼炭，實須練實，以綏其難。

translations.literal: South Central is exceedingly far, customs and rumors widely separated; barbarians and Liao craftily plunder; frontier folk suffer bitterly—there is real need for experienced men to pacify that difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: The far south is remote beyond measure; local ways and reports are cut off; barbarian raiders are cunning; frontier commoners are ground down—only seasoned officials can pacify that troubled land.

sentences.zh: 謂森之可交州刺史，天寶可寧州刺吏，庶足威懷荒表，肅清遐服。

translations.literal: It is proposed that Senzhi be made Governor of Jiaozhi and Tianbao Governor of Ning—this may suffice to awe and comfort the wild frontier and to purge distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant proposes appointing Senzhi Governor of Jiaozhi and Tianbao Governor of Ning—so doing may suffice to inspire awe and win over the frontier and to bring order to distant lands.

sentences.zh: 昔魏戊之賢，功存薦士；

translations.literal: In olden times Wei Wu's worth lay in recommending able men;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the merit of Wei Wu lay in recommending worthy men;

sentences.zh: 趙武之明，事彰管庫。

translations.literal: Zhao Wu's clarity was shown in affairs of the storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: The discernment of Duke Wu of Zhao was proved in managing the granaries.

sentences.zh: 臣識愧前良，理謝先哲，率舉所知，仰酬採訪，退懼瞽言，無足甄獎。

translations.literal: Your servant's knowledge falls short of former worthies, reasoning less than sages of old; I have straightforwardly recommended those I know to respond to the imperial inquiry; yet I fear blind words are unworthy of selection and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's discernment cannot match the worthies of old, nor my reasoning the sages before me; I have simply nominated those I know in answer to Your Majesty's call, yet I fear my ignorant remarks merit no selection or praise.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進位司空。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen he advanced to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 明年，大將軍彭城王義康有罪出藩，征義恭為侍中、都督揚、南徐、兗三州諸軍事、司徒、錄尚書，領太子太傅，持節如故，給班劍二十人，置仗加兵。

translations.literal: Next year the Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang, guilty of offense, was sent out from the capital; Yigong was summoned as Palace Attendant, Commander over the military affairs of Yang, Southern Xu, and Yan provinces, Minister over the Masses, Recorder of the Master of Writing, concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir, with credential staff as before, granted twenty ceremonial guards with drawn swords, and armed forces were added.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Prince Yikang of Pengcheng, Grand General, was found guilty and banished from court; Yigong was recalled as Palace Attendant, commander of Yang, Southern Xu, and Yan, Minister over the Masses, Chief Administrator of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Tutor to the Heir, his commission unchanged, with twenty guards bearing ritual swords, and additional troops were assigned.

sentences.zh: 明年，解督南兗。

translations.literal: The next year he relinquished command of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he gave up his supervision of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，進太尉，領司徒，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to Grand Commandant, retaining the post of Minister over the Masses; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one he rose to Grand Commandant while keeping the Ministry over the Masses; all other titles remained as before.

sentences.zh: 義恭既小心恭慎，且戒義康之失，雖為總錄，奉行文書而已，故太祖安之。

translations.literal: Yigong was careful and reverent, and mindful of Yikang's failures; though chief recorder he merely carried out documents—therefore Emperor Wen was at ease with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong acted with cautious reverence and took warning from Yikang's mistakes; though he held overall charge of the secretariat he only executed paperwork, and so Taizu trusted him.

sentences.zh: 相府年給錢二千萬，它物倍此，而義恭性奢，用常不足，太祖又別給錢年千萬。

translations.literal: The chief minister's office received twenty million cash annually, other goods at double that, yet Yigong was extravagant and his expenses often fell short; the Emperor additionally granted him ten million cash each year.
translations.idiomatic: The prime minister's household was allotted twenty million cash per year and twice that in other goods, but Yigong lived lavishly and still ran short; Taizu therefore added an annual grant of ten million cash.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he took charge as Chancellor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six he assumed the chancellorship of the National University.

sentences.zh: 時有獻五百里馬者，以賜義恭。

translations.literal: When someone presented a horse said to run five hundred li a day, it was given to Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: Someone offered a horse reputed to cover five hundred li in a day, and it was bestowed on Yigong.

sentences.zh: 二十七年春，索虜寇豫州，太祖因此欲開定河、洛。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-seventh year the Northern Wei raided Yuzhou; the Emperor therefore wished to reopen the campaign to secure the Yellow and Luo rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year twenty-seven the Wei invaders struck Yuzhou, and Taizu therefore intended to launch operations to settle the He and Luo region.

sentences.zh: 其秋，以義恭總統群帥，出鎮彭城，解國子祭酒。

translations.literal: That autumn Yigong was placed in overall command of the generals and went out to hold Pengcheng; he relinquished the university chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Yigong took supreme command of the armies and marched out to garrison Pengcheng, resigning the university post.

sentences.zh: 虜遂深入，徑至瓜步，義恭與世祖閉彭城自守。

translations.literal: The invaders pressed deep inland, reaching Guabu directly; Yigong and Emperor Xiaowu shut Pengcheng and held it.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy drove far inland, coming straight to Guabu; Yigong and Xiaowu sealed themselves inside Pengcheng to defend it.

sentences.zh: 二十八年春，虜退走，自彭城北過，義恭震懼不敢追。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-eighth year the invaders withdrew; passing north of Pengcheng, Yigong in shock and fear dared not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year twenty-eight the invaders retreated; as they passed north of Pengcheng, Yigong, shaken with fear, did not dare give chase.

sentences.zh: 其日，民有告：「虜驅廣陵民萬餘口，夕應宿安王陂，去城數十里。

translations.literal: That day a commoner reported: "The invaders are driving more than ten thousand people of Guangling; tonight they should camp at the Prince of An's dyke, several tens of li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: That same day a civilian reported: "The enemy is herding more than ten thousand people from Guangling; they ought to camp tonight at Anwang Dyke, a few dozen li from the city.

sentences.zh: 今追之，可悉得。」

translations.literal: If we pursue now, we can take them all."
translations.idiomatic: Pursue them now and we can recover them all."

sentences.zh: 諸將並請，義恭又禁不許。

translations.literal: All the generals requested it, but Yigong again forbade it and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders all urged pursuit, but Yigong once more refused permission.

sentences.zh: 經宿，太祖遣驛至，使悉力急追。

translations.literal: After one night Taizu sent a courier post-haste, ordering them to pursue with all strength and speed.
