translations.idiomatic: After a night's delay Taizu dispatched a relay rider ordering an all-out urgent pursuit.

sentences.zh: 義恭乃遣鎮軍司馬檀和之向蕭城。

translations.literal: Yigong then sent the Army Aide of the Garrison Forces Tan Hezhi toward Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Yigong send Tan Hezhi, army aide of the garrison command, toward Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 虜先已聞知，乃盡殺所驅廣陵民，輕騎引去。

translations.literal: The invaders had already heard; they killed all the Guangling people they had driven and fled lightly mounted.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had already learned of the pursuit; they slaughtered every Guangling captive they had driven along and fled with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 初，虜深入，上慮義恭不能固彭城，備加誡敕。

translations.literal: When the invaders first penetrated deep, the Emperor feared Yigong could not hold Pengcheng firm and added stern admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the enemy thrust deep inland, the throne feared Yigong might not hold Pengcheng and sent repeated stern warnings.

sentences.zh: 義恭答曰：「臣未能臨瀚海，濟居延，庶免劉仲奔逃之恥。」

translations.literal: Yigong replied: "Your servant has not yet reached the Han Sea or crossed to Juyan, but I hope at least to avoid the shame of Liu Zhong's flight."
translations.idiomatic: Yigong answered: "I have not yet marched to the Han Sea or crossed to Juyan, but I hope at least to escape the disgrace of Liu Zhong's rout."

sentences.zh: 及虜至，義恭果走，賴眾議得停，事在《張暢傳》。

translations.literal: When the invaders arrived, Yigong indeed fled; only by the assembly's counsel was he stopped—the affair is in the biography of Zhang Chang.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy arrived Yigong did flee; he was halted only because the council intervened—the account is in the biography of Zhang Chang.

sentences.zh: 降義恭號驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司，餘悉如故。

translations.literal: His title was reduced to General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Master with the same ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted in rank to General of Agile Cavalry with an office matching the Three Excellencies in ceremony; everything else stayed the same.

sentences.zh: 魯郡孔子舊庭有柏樹二十四株，經歷漢、晉，其大連抱。

translations.literal: In the old court of Confucius in Lu commandery there were twenty-four cypress trees, passing through Han and Jin, their trunks so large several men could embrace them.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient grove of Confucius in Lu had twenty-four cypress trees, standing since Han and Jin times, each trunk requiring several men to encircle.

sentences.zh: 有二株先折倒，士人崇敬，莫之敢犯，義恭悉遣人伐取，父老莫不歎息。

translations.literal: Two trees had earlier broken and fallen; the people revered them and none dared violate them—Yigong sent men to cut and take them all, and elders everywhere sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Two had already toppled; the people held them sacred and none would touch them—yet Yigong had them all felled and carried off, and the elders lamented.

sentences.zh: 又以本官領南兗州刺史，增督南兗、豫、徐、兗、青、冀、司、雍、秦、幽、并十一州諸軍事，并前十三州，移鎮盱眙。

translations.literal: He also held his original office while taking the governorship of Southern Yan, with added command over eleven provinces' military affairs—Southern Yan, Yu, Xu, Yan, Qing, Ji, Si, Yong, Qin, You, and Bing—together with the previous thirteen; he moved his headquarters to Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He retained his prior rank while becoming Governor of Southern Yan and gained supervision of eleven more provinces' armies; in all thirteen—moving his command to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 修治館宇，擬制東城。

translations.literal: He repaired and built halls and lodges, modeling them on the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He renovated his residence and offices, patterning them after the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 二十九年冬，還朝，上以御所乘蒼鷹船上迎之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-ninth year he returned to court; the Emperor met him aboard the dark hawk ship he himself rode.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of year twenty-nine he returned to the capital; Xiaowu came out on the imperial dark-hawk boat to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 遭太妃憂，改授大將軍、都督揚、南徐二州諸軍事、南徐州刺史，持節、侍中、錄尚書、太子太傅如故。

translations.literal: Upon the mourning for his mother the Princess Consort, he was reassigned Grand General, Commander over the military affairs of Yang and Southern Xu, Governor of Southern Xu, with credential staff, Palace Attendant, Recorder of the Master of Writing, and Grand Tutor of the Heir unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother the imperial consort died, he was reassigned as Grand General and commander of Yang and Southern Xu, Governor of Southern Xu, keeping his commission, palace attendance, secretariat duties, and tutorship of the Heir.

sentences.zh: 還鎮東府。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison the Eastern Palace headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He went back to hold the Eastern Palace residence.

sentences.zh: 辭侍中，未拜。

translations.literal: He declined the Palace Attendant post and was not invested.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned the palace attendant title and never took the appointment.

sentences.zh: 值元兇肆逆，其日劭召義恭。

translations.literal: When the arch-criminal committed his outrage, that day Liu Shao summoned Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper struck, Liu Shao summoned Yigong that very day.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔召太子及諸王，各有常人，慮有詐妄致害者。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had summoned the Heir and the princes, each with a regular attendant, fearing fraud that might bring harm.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when the throne summoned the Heir and the princes, each was to bring his usual courier, lest a forged summons bring disaster.

sentences.zh: 至是義恭求常所遣傳詔，劭遣之而後入。

translations.literal: Now Yigong asked for the usual imperial messenger; Shao sent him and only then entered.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong demanded the regular palace messenger; Shao provided one, and only then did Yigong enter.

sentences.zh: 義恭請罷兵，凡府內兵仗，並送還臺。

translations.literal: Yigong requested that troops be stood down; all weapons and armor within the princely residence were sent back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong asked that military action cease; every weapon in his household was returned to the central arsenal.

sentences.zh: 進位太保，進督會州諸軍事，服侍中服，又領大宗師。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Guardian, with added command over Huizhou military affairs, wearing palace attendant dress, and also taking charge as Grand Preceptor of the lineage.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Grand Guardian, gained command of Huizhou's armies, wore court dress as a palace attendant, and was named Grand Preceptor of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 世祖入討，劭疑義恭有異志，使入住尚書下省，分諸子並住神虎門外侍中下省。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu marched to punish Shao, Shao suspected Yigong of disloyal intent and had him stay in the lower offices of the Ministry of Writing; his sons were separated to wait outside the Shenhu Gate at the lower palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiaowu advanced to suppress Shao, Shao doubted Yigong's loyalty and confined him in the lower secretariat; all his sons were quartered outside Shenhu Gate under guard.

sentences.zh: 劭聞世祖已次近路，欲悉力逆之，決戰中道。

translations.literal: Shao heard Xiaowu had already halted on the near road and wished to muster all strength to oppose him in decisive battle on the way.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Xiaowu's vanguard was already close, Shao wanted to throw every force against him in a mid-route showdown.

sentences.zh: 義恭慮世祖船乘陋小，劭豕突中流，容能為患，乃進說曰：「割棄南岸，柵斷石頭，此先朝舊法；

translations.literal: Yigong feared Xiaowu's boats were small and shabby; Shao might charge like a boar midstream and could become a hazard—he therefore advised, saying: "Abandon the south bank, palisade and block Shitou—this is the former dynasty's old method;
translations.idiomatic: Yigong worried Xiaowu's fleet was flimsy; Shao might ram them mid-river and cause havoc—so he urged: "Give up the south bank and fortify Shitou—That was our forebears' tried tactic;

sentences.zh: 以逸待勞，不憂不破也。」

translations.literal: wait at ease for the weary foe—there is no worry of not breaking them."
translations.idiomatic: rest while the enemy exhausts themselves—you need not fear failing to crush them."

sentences.zh: 劭從之。

translations.literal: Shao followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Shao accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 世祖前鋒至新亭，劭挾義恭出戰，恆錄在左右，故不能自拔。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu's vanguard reached Xinting, Shao forced Yigong out to fight, always keeping him at his side, so he could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: As Xiaowu's van reached Xinting, Shao dragged Yigong into battle, never letting him leave his side, so he could not slip away.

sentences.zh: 戰敗，使義恭於東堂簡將。

translations.literal: After defeat Shao had Yigong select generals at the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout Shao made Yigong pick commanders in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 義恭先使人具船於東冶渚，因單馬南奔。

translations.literal: Yigong had already sent men to prepare boats at Dongye Ford; he then fled south alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong had already ordered boats readied at Dongye Ford; he bolted south on one horse.

sentences.zh: 始濟淮，追騎已至北岸，僅然得免。

translations.literal: Just as he crossed the Huai, pursuing horsemen had reached the north bank—he barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He had just crossed the Huai when pursuers appeared on the north bank—he escaped only by a hair.

sentences.zh: 劭大怒，遣始興王濬就西省殺義恭十二子。

translations.literal: Shao in great rage sent Prince Jun of Shixing to the western offices to kill Yigong's twelve sons.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Shao dispatched Prince Jun of Shixing to the western palace to execute Yigong's twelve sons.

sentences.zh: 世祖時在新林浦，義恭既至，上表勸世祖即位，曰：「臣聞治亂無兆，倚伏相因，乾靈降禍，二凶極逆，深酷巨痛，終古未有。

translations.literal: Xiaowu was then at Xinlin Ford; when Yigong arrived he submitted a memorial urging Xiaowu to take the throne, saying: "Your servant has heard that order and chaos have no omens, fortune and misfortune follow each other; Heaven's spirit sends calamity—two criminals at the utmost of rebellion, deep and cruel beyond all pain, never before in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu was at Xinlin Ford when Yigong arrived and memorialized urging him to ascend, saying: "I hear that order and chaos announce no signs in advance, that rise and fall depend on one another; Heaven has sent down disaster—two fiends at the peak of treason, agony deeper than any age has known.

sentences.zh: 陛下忠孝自天，赫然電發，投袂泣血，四海順軌，是以諸侯雲赴，數均八百；

translations.literal: Your Majesty's loyalty and filial piety come from Heaven; you flashed forth like lightning, shook your sleeves and wept blood—the four seas followed your track; therefore the feudal lords came like clouds, their number matching the eight hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's loyalty and filial piety are heaven-sent; you erupted like lightning, flung aside your sleeves and wept blood—the realm fell in behind you; lords gathered like clouds, eight hundred strong;

sentences.zh: 義奮之旅，其會如林。

translations.literal: hosts fired by righteousness gathered like a forest.
translations.idiomatic: righteous armies mustered thick as a forest.

sentences.zh: 神祚明德，有所底止，而沖居或躍，未登天祚，非所以嚴重宗社，紹延七百。

translations.literal: The divine mandate and bright virtue have their resting place, yet dwelling in modesty one may still leap—not yet ascending heaven's throne; this is not how to solemnly uphold the altars and continue the seven hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's favor and bright virtue have found their object, yet you still hold back from the throne; that is no way to secure the ancestral temples and carry on the dynasty's seven centuries.

sentences.zh: 昔張武抗辭，代王順請；

translations.literal: In olden times Zhang Wu resisted with words and the King of Dai yielded his plea;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zhang Wu declined in protest while the King of Dai yielded the throne at his urging;

sentences.zh: 耿純陳款，光武正位。

translations.literal: Geng Chun stated his loyalty and Emperor Guangwu took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Chun pledged his allegiance and Guangwu assumed the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 況今罪逆無親，惡盈釁滿，阻兵安忍，戮善崇奸，履地戴天，畢命俄頃；

translations.literal: How much more now when the guilty rebel has no kin, evil brims and omen overflows, they hold armies and indulge cruelty, slay the good and exalt the wicked, tread earth and wear heaven—life ends in an instant;
translations.idiomatic: All the more when the traitor stands utterly alone, his wickedness full to bursting, who keeps armies and delights in cruelty, kills the worthy and honors villains—under heaven and upon earth his life will end in a breath;

sentences.zh: 宜早定尊號，以固社稷。

translations.literal: the exalted title should early be fixed to secure the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: you should establish the imperial title at once to stabilize the realm.

sentences.zh: 景平之季，實惟樂推，王室之亂，天命有在，故抱拜兆於壓璧，赤龍表於霄徵。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jingping era it was truly the people's push; in the chaos of the royal house the mandate of Heaven had its place—therefore they bowed at the omen upon the jade disk and the red dragon appeared in the sky's sign.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of Jingping the people truly thrust the throne upon him; amid the royal house's turmoil Heaven's mandate was clear—hence the bow at the omen on the jade bi and the red dragon in the celestial signs.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大明無私，遠存家國七廟之靈，近哀黔首荼炭之切，時陟帝祚，永慰群心。

translations.literal: I consider that great brightness is without partiality; looking far, preserve the spirits of the seven temples of the house and state; looking near, pity the bitter suffering of the black-haired people—ascend the imperial throne in season and forever comfort all hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Great illumination knows no favoritism; honor the seven temples of our house, pity the people's torment—take the throne in good time and forever ease every heart.

sentences.zh: 臣負釁嬰罰，偷生人壤，幸及寬政，待罪有司，敢以漏刻視息，披露肝膽。」

translations.literal: Your servant bears guilt and infant punishment, stealing life upon the soil; fortunate to reach lenient rule, awaiting punishment before the officials—I dare not regard the dripping clepsydra and breathing, but lay bare liver and gall."
translations.idiomatic: I bear guilt and deserve death yet live on; thanks to Your Majesty's mercy I await judgment—I dare not merely watch the clock tick by, but expose my inmost heart."

sentences.zh: 世祖即祚，授使持節、侍中、都督揚、南徐二州諸軍事、太尉、錄尚書六條事、南徐、徐二州刺史，給鼓吹一部，班劍二十人；

translations.literal: Xiaowu immediately took the throne and appointed him Bearer of the Credential Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander over the military affairs of Yang and Southern Xu, Grand Commandant, Recorder of the six articles of the Master of Writing, Governor of Southern Xu and Xu, granted one set of ceremonial drums and horns, twenty ceremonial guards with drawn swords;
translations.idiomatic: The moment Xiaowu ascended he appointed Yigong Bearer of the Credential Staff, Palace Attendant, commander of Yang and Southern Xu, Grand Commandant, chief of the six secretariat bureaus, Governor of Southern Xu and Xu, with one drum-and-horn ensemble and twenty ritual sword guards;

sentences.zh: 又假黃鉞。

translations.literal: He was also lent the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: He was also granted the yellow battle-axe on loan.

sentences.zh: 事寧，進位太傅，領大司馬，增班劍為三十人。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was promoted to Grand Tutor, concurrently Grand Marshal, and ceremonial guards increased to thirty.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was restored he rose to Grand Tutor and Grand Marshal, with thirty ritual sword guards.

sentences.zh: 以在藩所服玉環大綬賜之。

translations.literal: The jade ring and great ribbon he had worn in his princely post were bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: He received as gifts the jade ring and great sash he had worn as prince.

sentences.zh: 增封二千戶。

translations.literal: His fief was increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand households were added to his enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 上不欲致禮太傅，諷有司奏曰：「聖旨謙光，尊師重道，欲致拜太傅，斯誠弘茲遠風，敦闡盛則。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not wish to perform obeisance to the Grand Tutor and hinted that the officials should memorialize, saying: "The sacred intent is modest and honors the teacher and esteems the Way, wishing to perform obeisance to the Grand Tutor—this is truly to expand the far-reaching wind and thickly proclaim the flourishing norm.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu did not wish to bow to his Grand Tutor and prompted the bureaucracy to memorialize: "Your Majesty's humility honors your teacher and the Way; you wish to bow to the Grand Tutor—truly to spread lofty custom and affirm flourishing rule.

sentences.zh: 然周之師保，實稱三吏，晉因於魏，特加其禮。

translations.literal: Yet Zhou's teacher and guardian were truly called the three officers; Jin followed Wei and specially added the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Zhou the tutor and guardian were called the three administrators; Jin followed Wei and added special ceremony.

sentences.zh: 帝道嚴極，既有常尊，考之史載，未見茲典。

translations.literal: The imperial Way is stern and supreme, having its fixed exalted station; examining the historical records, this ceremony is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial dignity stands supreme with its fixed honors; history records no such precedent.

sentences.zh: 故卞壼、孫楚並謂人君無降尊之義。

translations.literal: Therefore Bian Hu and Sun Chu both said that a ruler has no principle of lowering his dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Hence Bian Hu and Sun Chu both held that a sovereign should not demean his rank.

sentences.zh: 遠稽聖典，近即群心，臣等參議謂不應有加拜之禮。」

translations.literal: Examining far the sage canon and taking near the hearts of the multitude, we your servants jointly deliberated and hold that there should not be the ceremony of added obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Searching antiquity's classics and weighing the people's mind, we jointly advise against the added bow.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「闇薄纂統，實憑師範，思盡虔恭，以承道訓。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Dim and shallow in succeeding to the succession, I truly rely on the teacher's model; I think to exhaust reverence and respect to receive the Way's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Shallow as I am upon the throne, I truly depend on my teacher's example; I mean to show utmost reverence and receive his instruction.

sentences.zh: 所奏稽諸往代，謂無拜禮，據文既明，便從所執。」

translations.literal: Your memorial checks against former ages and says there is no bowing ceremony; the text being clear, follow what you hold."
translations.idiomatic: Your report cites past ages and finds no bowing rite; the wording is clear—do as you advise."

sentences.zh: 世祖立太子，東宮文案，使先經義恭。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu established the Heir, Eastern Palace documents were first routed through Yigong.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu named the Heir, all Eastern Palace papers passed through Yigong first.

sentences.zh: 孝建元年，南郡王義宣、臧質、魯爽等反，加黃鉞，白直百人入六門。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian, Prince Yixuan of Nanjun, Zang Zhi, Lu Shuang, and others rebelled; the yellow battle-axe was added, and a hundred white-guard troops entered the six gates.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian year one, Prince Yixuan of Nanjun, Zang Zhi, Lu Shuang, and others rose in rebellion; Yigong received the yellow battle-axe and a hundred household guards entered the six palace gates.

sentences.zh: 事平，以臧質七百里馬賜義恭，又增封二千戶。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled the seven-hundred-li horse of Zang Zhi was given to Yigong, and his fief was again increased by two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After the revolt was crushed Zang Zhi's seven-hundred-li horse was bestowed on Yigong, and two thousand more households were added to his fief.

sentences.zh: 世祖以義宣亂逆，由於強盛，至是欲削弱王侯。

translations.literal: Xiaowu considered that Yixuan's rebellion and treason came from excessive power; at this time he wished to weaken the princes and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu believed Yixuan's revolt stemmed from princely power grown too great; now he meant to curtail the feudal lords.

sentences.zh: 義恭希旨，乃上表省錄尚書，曰：「臣聞天地設位，三極同序，皇王化則，九官咸事。

translations.literal: Yigong caught the intent and submitted a memorial to abolish the Recorder of the Master of Writing, saying: "Your servant has heard that Heaven and Earth set their positions and the three poles share one order; the king's transforming norm—nine officers all have their tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Reading the throne's mind, Yigong memorialized to eliminate the chief secretariat post, saying: "I hear Heaven and Earth fix their stations and the three ultimates share one sequence; the king's transforming model puts all nine ministers to work.

sentences.zh: 時亮之績，昭於《虞典》；

translations.literal: Shi Liang's achievements shine in the Canon of Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Liang's feats shine in the Documents of Yu;

sentences.zh: 論道之風，宣於周載。

translations.literal: the wind of discussing the Way is proclaimed in Zhou's records.
translations.idiomatic: the tradition of deliberating the Way resounds in Zhou's annals.

sentences.zh: 台輔之設，坐調陰陽，元、凱之置，起釐百揆。

translations.literal: The setting of terrace and aide adjusts yin and yang; the placing of Yuan and Kai initiates ordering the hundred duties.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers' offices harmonize yin and yang; appointing Yuan and Kai begins ordering the hundred affairs.

sentences.zh: 所以欒鍼矢言，侵官是誡；

translations.literal: Therefore Luan Zhen spoke bluntly—encroaching on office is the warning;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Luan Zhen spoke plainly—usurping another's office is the lesson;

sentences.zh: 陳平抗辭，匪職罔答。

translations.literal: Chen Ping resisted with words—without duty there is no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping declined on principle—without proper office one does not reply.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦後，庶僚稍改。

translations.literal: Han followed Qin afterward and the multitude of officials was slightly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Han inherited from Qin and gradually reshaped the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 爵因時變，任與世移，總錄之制，本非舊體，列代相沿，茲仍未革。

translations.literal: Ranks changed with the times, duties shifted with the age—the system of chief recorder was originally not the old form; dynasties passed it along and it has still not been reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Titles shifted with the times, roles with the era—the chief recorder's office was never ancient; dynasty after dynasty kept it, unreformed still.

sentences.zh: 今皇家中造，事遵前文，宜憲章先代，證文古則，停省條錄，以依昔典。

translations.literal: Now the royal house is newly rebuilt, affairs following former text—it should take the statutes of former ages and verify the ancient norms, stop and abolish the recorder's articles, to follow the former canon.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty is newly restored and should follow precedent—let us restore ancient statutes, abolish the recorder's portfolio, and return to the old canon.

sentences.zh: 使物競思存，人懷勤壹，則名實靡愆，庸節必紀。

translations.literal: Let things compete in thought of preservation and men cherish unified diligence—then name and reality will not err and ordinary integrity will surely be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Let every office strive to endure and every man work with single purpose—then titles will match duties and merit will be recorded.

sentences.zh: 臣謬典國重，虛荷崇位，興替宜知，敢不輸盡。」

translations.literal: Your servant wrongly holds the state's weight, bearing the lofty post in vain—rise and fall should be known; how dare I not exhaust my effort."
translations.idiomatic: I wrongly hold the state's heavy charge and a lofty seat I do not deserve—I know what rise and fall require; how could I hold back?"

sentences.zh: 上從其議。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed this proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又與驃騎大將軍竟陵王誕奏曰：「臣聞佾懸有數，等級異儀，佩笏有制，卑高殊序。

translations.literal: He also jointly memorialized with General of Agile Cavalry and Grand General Prince Dan of Jingling, saying: "Your servant has heard that the ya suspension has its number, ranks and grades differ in ceremony; wearing the tablet has its rule, low and high differ in order.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Prince Dan of Jingling, General of Agile Cavalry and Grand General, he submitted: "I hear the ya bells have fixed numbers, ranks differ in ritual; tablet and scepter follow rules, high and low keep distinct order.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋上哲之洪謨，範世之明訓。

translations.literal: This is the great plan of the supreme sages, the bright instruction for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the supreme sages' grand design, the bright lesson for all ages.

sentences.zh: 而時至彌流，物無不弊，僭侈由俗，軌度非古。

translations.literal: Yet as time reaches its full flow nothing is without decay; extravagance follows custom, standards and measures are not ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Yet time ever flows and nothing escapes decay; extravagance follows fashion while standards are no longer those of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 晉代東徙，舊法淪落，侯牧典章，稍與事廣，名實一差，難以卒變，章服崇濫，多歷年所。

translations.literal: When Jin moved east the old laws sank away; the marquises' and prefects' statutes gradually widened with affairs—once name and reality differed, sudden change was hard; excessive robes and ranks have lasted many years.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern flight of Jin the old regulations lapsed; lords' and governors' regalia slowly swelled with power—once names and reality diverged, change was hard; lavish dress and titles have piled up for years.

sentences.zh: 今樞機更造，皇風載新，耗弊未充，百用思約，宜備品式之律，以定損厭之條。

translations.literal: Now the pivot is remade and the imperial wind bears anew; waste and exhaustion are not yet filled, a hundred uses seek thrift—it should prepare laws of grades and types to fix rules of reduction and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The court is remade and imperial custom renewed; coffers are still empty and every expense cries for thrift—we should codify grades and fix rules of reduction.

sentences.zh: 臣等地居枝昵，位參台輔，遵正之首，請以爵先；

translations.literal: We your servants in place are branch and kin, rank joining terrace and aide—in observing correctness the request should begin with rank first;
translations.idiomatic: We stand as imperial kin and chief ministers—in upholding propriety let rank lead the way;

sentences.zh: 致貶之端，宜從戚始。

translations.literal: the starting point of imposing demotion should begin with kin.
translations.idiomatic: and let the first cuts fall upon us, the emperor's kin.

sentences.zh: 輒因暇日，共參愚懷，應加省易，謹陳九事。

translations.literal: They therefore on a free day jointly submitted their humble thoughts on what should be simplified and reduced, respectfully presenting nine items.
translations.idiomatic: On a day of leisure they pooled their modest views on what ought to be trimmed, and respectfully set forth nine proposals.

sentences.zh: 雖懼匪衷，庶竭微款。

translations.literal: Though fearing it is not sincere, they hoped to exhaust their slight loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Though doubting their hearts are equal to the task, they hoped at least to offer what little sincerity they had.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下聽覽之餘，薄垂昭納，則上下相安，表裏和穆矣。」

translations.literal: They bow and wish that after Your Majesty hears and reads, you will lightly bestow clear acceptance—then above and below will be at peace, outer and inner harmonious."
translations.idiomatic: They pray that after Your Majesty has heard them, you will graciously accept—so that court and realm may rest secure and inner and outer harmony prevail."

sentences.zh: 詔付外詳。

translations.literal: The edict ordered it sent out for detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed that the memorial be referred to the outer offices for detailed deliberation.

sentences.zh: 有司奏曰：

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 車服以庸，《虞書》茂典；

translations.literal: Chariots and robes follow merit—the Canon of Yu's flourishing canon;
translations.idiomatic: Chariots and dress reward merit—so the Canon of Yu teaches;

sentences.zh: 名器慎假，《春秋》明誡。

translations.literal: titles and vessels are cautiously lent—the Spring and Autumn's clear admonition.
translations.idiomatic: titles and insignia must be granted with care—so the Spring and Autumn warns.

sentences.zh: 是以尚方所制，漢有嚴律，諸侯竊服，雖親必罪。

translations.literal: Therefore what the Imperial Workshop made—Han had strict laws; feudal lords who usurped dress, though kin, were surely punished.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the imperial workshops had strict Han statutes: any lord who stole princely regalia, however close in kin, was punished.

sentences.zh: 降於頃世，下僭滋極。

translations.literal: Descending to recent generations, lower usurpation grew to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times the lower ranks' presumption has grown extreme.

sentences.zh: 器服裝飾，樂舞音容，通於王公，達于眾庶。

translations.literal: Vessels, dress, ornament, music, dance, sound, and bearing reached princes and dukes and extended to the common multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Regalia, dress, ornament, music, dance, and bearing alike reached princes and commoners.

sentences.zh: 上下無辨，民志靡壹。

translations.literal: Above and below had no distinction; the people's will was not unified.
translations.idiomatic: High and low were indistinguishable; popular sentiment lost its single focus.

sentences.zh: 義恭所陳，實允禮度。

translations.literal: What Yigong stated truly accorded with ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong's proposals truly matched ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 九條之格，猶有未盡，謹共附益，凡二十四條：

translations.literal: The nine-article rules still had what was not exhausted; they respectfully jointly added and enriched them—twenty-four articles in all:
translations.idiomatic: The nine articles still left gaps; the offices jointly supplemented them—for twenty-four articles in all:

sentences.zh: 聽事不得南向坐，施帳并。

translations.literal: In the audience hall one may not sit facing south, with canopy and together.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall of business one may not sit facing south under a full canopy.

sentences.zh: 藩國官，正冬不得跣登國殿，及夾侍國師傳令及油戟；

translations.literal: Princely state officials in mid-winter may not go barefoot to ascend the state hall, nor flank the state preceptor in transmitting orders and oil halberds;
translations.idiomatic: Princely officials in mid-winter may not enter the state hall barefoot, nor flank the tutor when bearing orders or oil halberds;

sentences.zh: 公主王妃傳令，不得朱服；

translations.literal: imperial princesses and princes' consorts transmitting orders may not wear vermilion dress;
translations.idiomatic: when princesses or princes' wives relay orders they may not wear vermilion robes;

sentences.zh: 輿不得重棡；

translations.literal: carriages may not have double crossbeams;
translations.idiomatic: carriages may not use double crossbeams;

sentences.zh: 鄣扇不得雉尾；

translations.literal: screen fans may not have pheasant tails;
translations.idiomatic: processional screens may not bear pheasant-tail plumes;

sentences.zh: 劍不得鹿盧形；

translations.literal: swords may not be in the deer-antler form;
translations.idiomatic: swords may not take the deer-antler shape;

sentences.zh: 槊眊不得孔雀白氅；

translations.literal: spear pennants may not have peacock white mantles;
translations.idiomatic: spear banners may not carry peacock-feather white mantles;

sentences.zh: 夾轂隊不得絳襖；

translations.literal: flanking-the-hub escorts may not wear crimson jackets;
translations.idiomatic: hub-guard escorts may not wear crimson coats;

sentences.zh: 平乘誕馬不得過二匹；

translations.literal: plain chariots and parade horses may not exceed two horses;
translations.idiomatic: light carts and parade mounts may not exceed two horses;

sentences.zh: 胡伎不得綵衣；

translations.literal: barbarian performers may not wear colored dress;
translations.idiomatic: non-Chinese entertainers may not wear brocade dress;

sentences.zh: 舞伎正冬著祍衣，不得裝面；

translations.literal: dancing girls in mid-winter wear lined garments and may not apply face makeup;
translations.idiomatic: dancers in mid-winter wear padded robes and may not paint their faces;

sentences.zh: 冬會不得鐸舞、杯柈舞；

translations.literal: winter assemblies may not include bell dance or cup-tray dance;
translations.idiomatic: winter gatherings may not feature bell dances or cup-and-tray dances;

sentences.zh: 長蹺、透狹、舒丸劍、博山、緣大橦、升五案，自非正冬會奏舞曲，不得舞；

translations.literal: long stilts, narrow passage, sword-ball, incense mountain, large pole with ropes, ascending five tables—unless at the mid-winter assembly when dance music is performed, these dances are not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: long stilts, tight-rope acts, sword-juggling, censer mountains, rope poles, and five-table acrobatics may be danced only at the mid-winter assembly when court dance music is played;

sentences.zh: 諸妃主不得著緄帶；

translations.literal: all consorts and princesses may not wear cord belts;
translations.idiomatic: consorts and princesses may not wear corded sashes;

sentences.zh: 信幡非台省官悉用絳；

translations.literal: credential banners—unless terrace or provincial officials, all use crimson;
translations.idiomatic: credential banners: all but central and provincial officials must use crimson;

sentences.zh: 郡縣內史相及封內官長，於其封君，既非在三，罷官則不復追敬，不合稱臣，宜止下官而已；

translations.literal: prefectural and district internal historians and magistrates and chief officials within the fief toward their enfeoffed lord—since they are not among the three ranks, once removed from office they no longer pursue reverence; it is not fitting to call themselves ministers; they should stop at "lower official" only;
translations.idiomatic: prefectural magistrates and fief officials toward their enfeoffed lord—no longer in the three highest ranks after leaving office, they should not call themselves "your minister" but only "your lower official";

sentences.zh: 諸鎮常行，車前後不得過六隊，白直夾轂，不在其限。

translations.literal: garrison posts on regular travel—before and behind the carriage may not exceed six squads; white-guard flanking the hub is not within this limit.
translations.idiomatic: on routine marches from garrison posts, escorts before and behind the carriage may not exceed six squads; white-guard hub escorts are excepted.

sentences.zh: 刀不得過銀銅為飾；

translations.literal: Blades may not have more than silver and copper for ornament;
translations.idiomatic: Blades may use only silver and copper for ornament, no more;

sentences.zh: 諸王女封縣主，諸王子孫襲封之王妃及封侯者夫人行，並不得鹵簿；

translations.literal: princes' daughters enfeoffed as district mistresses, princes' grandsons and heirs' enfeoffed princes' consorts and those enfeoffed as marquises' wives on travel—all may not use full guard of honor;
translations.idiomatic: princes' daughters made district ladies, heirs' consorts, and marquises' wives on the road may not deploy full guard of honor;

sentences.zh: 諸王子繼體為王者，婚葬吉凶，悉依諸國公侯之禮，不得同皇弟皇子。

translations.literal: princes' sons who succeed as kings—in weddings, funerals, and omens they all follow the rites of feudal dukes and marquises and may not be the same as the Emperor's younger brothers and sons.
translations.idiomatic: princes' sons who inherit princely rank must follow ducal and marquis rites for weddings and funerals, not those of the Emperor's brothers and sons.

sentences.zh: 車非軺車，不得油幢；

translations.literal: Carriages that are not light post chariots may not have oil banners;
translations.idiomatic: Carriages other than light post chariots may not bear oiled banners;

sentences.zh: 平乘船皆下兩頭作露平形，不得擬象龍舟，悉不得朱油；

translations.literal: plain riding boats all have exposed flat ends at bow and stern and may not imitate dragon boats; none may use vermilion oil;
translations.idiomatic: flat-bottom boats must have plain exposed ends and may not mimic dragon boats or use vermilion lacquer;

sentences.zh: 帳鉤不得作五花及豎筍形。

translations.literal: canopy hooks may not be made in five-flower or vertical bamboo-shoot form.
translations.idiomatic: canopy hooks may not take five-petal or upright bamboo-shoot shapes.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted approval.

sentences.zh: 是歲十一月，還鎮京口。

translations.literal: That year in the eleventh month he returned to garrison Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year he returned to his post at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 二年春，進督東、南兗二州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year he was advanced to command Eastern Yan and Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year two he gained supervision of Eastern and Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 其冬，徵為揚州刺史，餘如故。

translations.literal: That winter he was summoned as Governor of Yangzhou; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was recalled as Governor of Yangzhou; other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 加入朝不趨，贊拜不名，劍履上殿，固辭殊禮。

translations.literal: Added: on entering court no need to hurry, in laudatory bow no need to speak the name, sword and shoes in the hall—he firmly declined these special honors.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted exemption from hurrying at court, from having his name spoken in ceremonial praise, and the right to wear sword and shoes in the hall—all of which he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 又解持節、都督并侍中。

translations.literal: He also relinquished the credential staff, overall command, and Palace Attendant post.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave up his commission, overall military command, and palace attendance.

sentences.zh: 義恭撰《要記》五卷，起前漢訖晉太元，表上之，詔付秘閣。

translations.literal: Yigong compiled Essential Records in five scrolls, from Former Han through Jin's Taiyuan, submitted it in memorial, and an edict ordered it stored in the Secret Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong compiled the Essential Records in five juan, from Former Han through Jin's Taiyuan era, presented it to the throne, and an edict placed it in the Secret Archive.

sentences.zh: 時西陽王子尚有盛寵，義恭解揚州以避之，乃進位太宰，領司徒。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Zishang of Xiyang enjoyed great favor; Yigong relinquished Yangzhou to avoid conflict and was promoted to Grand Preceptor, concurrently Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zishang of Xiyang then held imperial favor; Yigong resigned Yangzhou to step aside and was promoted to Grand Preceptor while keeping the Ministry over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 義恭常慮為世祖所疑，及海陵王休茂於襄陽為亂，乃上表曰：

translations.literal: Yigong often feared suspicion from Xiaowu; when Prince Xiamao of Hailing rebelled at Xiangyang he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yigong constantly feared Xiaowu's mistrust; when Prince Xiamao of Hailing rose in rebellion at Xiangyang he memorialized, saying:

sentences.zh: 古先哲王，莫不廣植周親，以屏帝宇，諸侯受爵，亦願永固邦家。

translations.literal: The ancient sage kings all broadly planted Zhou kin to shield the imperial domain; feudal lords receiving ranks also wished to forever secure house and state.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sage-kings planted kinsmen widely to guard the throne; lords who received fiefs likewise hoped to secure their houses forever.

sentences.zh: 至有管蔡、梁燕，致禍周、漢，上乖顯授之恩，下亡血食之業。

translations.literal: Yet there were Guan and Cai, Liang and Yan, bringing calamity on Zhou and Han—above betraying the grace of manifest investiture, below losing the livelihood of blood sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guan and Cai, Liang and Yan brought disaster on Zhou and Han—betraying investiture above and forfeiting ancestral sacrifice below.

sentences.zh: 夫善積慶深，宜享長久，而歷代侯王，甚乎匹庶。

translations.literal: Deep accumulated good fortune should enjoy long endurance, yet generation after generation marquises and kings fared worse than commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Deep virtue ought to endure, yet generation after generation feudal lords fared worse than commoners.

sentences.zh: 豈異姓皆賢，宗室悉不賢。

translations.literal: Was it that non-kin were all worthy while the imperial clan were all unworthy?
translations.idiomatic: Were all outsiders worthy and every clansman unworthy?

sentences.zh: 由生於深宮，不睹稼穡，左右近習，未值田蘇，富貴驕奢，自然而至，聚毛折軸，遂乃危禍。

translations.literal: Because born in the deep palace they did not see sowing and reaping; close attendants at the side never met fields and mulberry; wealth, nobility, pride, and extravagance came naturally—gathering hairs breaks the axle, and thus came peril and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in palace depths they never saw the fields; attendants never knew rural toil—wealth and pride came naturally, hairs gathered until the axle snaps, and disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 漢之諸王，並置傅相，猶不得禁逆；

translations.literal: Han's princes all had tutors and chancellors appointed, yet could not forbid rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Han set tutors and chancellors over every prince, yet could not prevent treason;

sentences.zh: 七國連謀，實由強盛。

translations.literal: the Seven States' linked plot truly came from excessive power.
translations.idiomatic: the Rebellion of the Seven States stemmed truly from princely power grown too great.

sentences.zh: 晉氏列封，正足成永嘉之禍。

translations.literal: Jin's enfeoffments sufficed only to complete the disaster of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's feudal grants were just enough to bring on the Yongjia catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 尾大不掉，終古同疾，不有更張，則其源莫救。

translations.literal: A tail too large to wag—the same affliction in all ages; without further reform its source cannot be saved.
translations.idiomatic: When the tail grows too heavy to control—the malady is eternal; without reform the root cannot be cured.

sentences.zh: 日者庶人恃親，殆傾王業。

translations.literal: Recently commoners relying on kinship nearly overturned the royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Lately commoners trading on kinship nearly toppled the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 去歲西寇藉寵，幾敗皇基。

translations.literal: Last year the western rebel relied on favor and nearly ruined the imperial foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the western favorite nearly wrecked the imperial foundation.

sentences.zh: 不圖襄楚，復生今釁，良以地勝兵勇，獎成兇惡。

translations.literal: Who would have thought Xiang and Chu would again produce today's omen—truly because the land was strong and soldiers brave, rewards bred fierce wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: None expected Xiang-Chu to breed fresh trouble—terrain and troops were too strong, and favor bred bold villainy.

sentences.zh: 前事之不忘，後事之明兆。

translations.literal: Not forgetting former affairs is the clear omen of later affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He who forgets not the past reads the future's warning.

sentences.zh: 陛下大明紹祚，垂法萬葉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty in great brightness continues the succession, handing down law for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's bright succession casts law for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 臣年衰意塞，無所知解。

translations.literal: Your servant's years decline and intent is blocked, without knowledge or understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's years fail and my mind grows dull—I understand little.

sentences.zh: 忝皇族耆長，慚慨內深，思表管見，裨崇萬一。

translations.literal: I disgracefully am the clan's elder in years, ashamed and indignant within, thinking to express a tube's glimpse to assist and honor the one in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: As senior among the imperial kin I burn with shame and grief within, and offer this humble view to help in the smallest measure.

sentences.zh: 竊謂諸王貴重，不應居邊，至於華州優地，時可暫出。

translations.literal: I privately hold that the princes' nobility and weight should not dwell on the frontier; as for Huazhou's favored lands, they may temporarily go out.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that princes should not hold border commands; only for favored posts like Huazhou might they serve briefly.

sentences.zh: 既以有州，不須置府。

translations.literal: Since they already hold a province, there is no need to set up a princely office.
translations.idiomatic: Once they hold a province they need no separate princely headquarters.

sentences.zh: 若位登三事，止乎長史掾屬。

translations.literal: If rank reaches the three duties, stop at chief clerk and aides.
translations.idiomatic: If they reach the three highest offices, staff should stop at chief clerk and aides.

sentences.zh: 若宜鎮御，別差扞城大將。

translations.literal: If garrison defense is appropriate, separately appoint a great general to defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: If defense is required, appoint a separate garrison general.

sentences.zh: 若情樂沖虛，不宜逼以戎事。

translations.literal: If their inclination is serene emptiness, they should not be pressed with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If they prefer quiet study, do not force military duty on them.

sentences.zh: 若捨文好武，尤宜禁塞。

translations.literal: If they abandon letters for martial arts, especially forbid and block it.
translations.idiomatic: If they favor arms over learning, forbid it all the more.

sentences.zh: 僚佐文學，足充話言，游梁之徒，一皆勿許。

translations.literal: Literary aides suffice for conversation; wandering swordsmen—none should be permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Literary staff are enough for discourse; roaming bravos must not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 文武從鎮，以時休止，妻子室累，不煩自隨。

translations.literal: Civil and military followers at the garrison should rest by season; wives and household burdens need not follow in person.
translations.idiomatic: Retainers civil and military should rotate by season; families need not travel with them.

sentences.zh: 百僚修詣，宜遵晉令，悉須宣令齊到，備列賓主之則。

translations.literal: Officials' visits of respect should follow Jin's order—all must arrive when the announcement order comes, fully arrayed in guest and host rules.
translations.idiomatic: Official calls of respect should follow Jin statutes—all must arrive when summoned, observing full guest-and-host ritual.

sentences.zh: 衡泌之士，亦無煩干候貴王。

translations.literal: Recluses of Heng and Bi also need not trouble themselves to wait on noble princes.
translations.idiomatic: Hermits of the Heng and Bi sort need not wait upon princes.

sentences.zh: 器甲於私，為用蓋寡，自金銀裝刀劍戰具之服，皆應輸送還本。

translations.literal: Armor in private use is largely useless—gold and silver mounted swords, blades, and battle gear should all be sent back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Private arms serve little purpose—gold- and silver-mounted swords and war gear should all be returned to court.

sentences.zh: 曲突徙薪，防之有素，庶善者無懼，惡者止奸。

translations.literal: Bending the chimney and moving the firewood—with defense prepared beforehand, the good will have no fear and the wicked will stop their treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Straighten the flue and move the firewood—prepare in advance, and the worthy need not fear while villains cease their plots.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝即位，詔曰：「總錄之典，著自前代。

translations.literal: When Former Deposed Emperor took the throne, an edict said: "The canon of chief recorder is established from former generations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Deposed Emperor ascended, an edict read: "The chief recorder's office is an institution of former ages.

sentences.zh: 孝建始年，雖暫並省，而因革有宜，理存濟務。

translations.literal: From the first year of Xiaojian it was briefly abolished together, yet following change there is what is fitting—principle exists to aid affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xiaojian's first year it was briefly abolished, yet reform must suit the times—principle remains to serve affairs.

sentences.zh: 朕煢獨在躬，未涉政道，百揆庶務，允歸尊德。

translations.literal: I alone and orphaned in person have not yet entered the path of governance; the hundred duties and myriad affairs truly return to honored virtue.
translations.idiomatic: I stand orphaned upon the throne, untrained in rule; every duty truly rests on honored virtue.

sentences.zh: 太宰江夏王義恭新除中書監、太尉，地居宗重，受遺阿衡，實深憑倚，用康庶績，可錄尚書事，本官監、太宰、王如故；

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia Yigong, newly appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat and Grand Commandant, in place as clan weight, received the testament as pillar and balance—truly deeply relied upon to bring peace to myriad achievements; he may record Master of Writing affairs, original offices of Director, Grand Preceptor, and Prince unchanged;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, newly made Director of the Secretariat and Grand Commandant, weighty in the clan and entrusted as regent, may resume recording Secretariat affairs; his titles as Director, Grand Preceptor, and Prince stand unchanged;

sentences.zh: 侍中、驃騎大將軍、南兗州刺史、巴東郡開國公、新除尚書令元景，同稟顧誓，翼輔皇家，贊業宣風，繄公是賴。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry and Grand General, Governor of Southern Yan, Duke of Badong commandery with open state, newly appointed Master of Writing Yuan Jing—together bearing the testament care, assisting and supporting the imperial house, praising enterprise and proclaiming wind—truly relying on the duke.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Yuan Jing, General of Agile Cavalry, Governor of Southern Yan, Duke of Badong, newly Chief of the Masters of Writing—co-regent by testament, pillar of the house—

sentences.zh: 可即本號開府儀同三司，領兵置佐，一依舊准，領丹陽尹、侍中、領公如故。」

translations.literal: He may immediately with his original title have an office matching the Three Excellencies in ceremony, lead troops and set aides, all according to old standard, concurrently Governor of Danyang, Palace Attendant, and Duke unchanged."
translations.idiomatic: may at once hold an office matching the Three Excellencies in ceremony, command troops and staff per old precedent, and keep Danyang governorship, palace attendance, and ducal rank."

sentences.zh: 又增義恭班劍為四十人，更申殊禮之命。

translations.literal: He also increased Yigong's ceremonial guards to forty and renewed the order of special honors.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong's ritual sword guards were raised to forty and special honors were renewed.

sentences.zh: 固辭殊禮。

translations.literal: He firmly declined the special honors.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused the special honors.

sentences.zh: 義恭性嗜不恆，日時移變，自始至終，屢遷第宅。

translations.literal: Yigong's nature in appetites was inconstant; day and time shifted— from beginning to end he repeatedly moved residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong's tastes were fickle; as days passed he changed—throughout his life he moved house again and again.

sentences.zh: 與人遊款，意好亦多不終。

translations.literal: In befriending people his goodwill also often did not last to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Even friendships he made seldom lasted.

sentences.zh: 而奢侈無度，不愛財寶，左右親幸者，一日乞與，或至一二百萬；

translations.literal: Yet he was extravagant without measure and did not cherish treasure; close favorites on a single day might beg and receive one or two million;
translations.idiomatic: He spent without limit and cared nothing for wealth; a favorite might receive one or two million in a single day;

sentences.zh: 小有忤意，輒追奪之。

translations.literal: if slightly displeased, he would pursue and seize it back.
translations.idiomatic: yet at the slightest offense he would seize it all back.

sentences.zh: 大明時，資供豐厚，而用常不足，賒市百姓物，無錢可還，民有通辭求錢者，輒題後作「原」字。

translations.literal: In the Daming era supplies were rich and thick yet expenses often fell short; he bought commoners' goods on credit with no money to repay—when people pressed for payment he would write "forgiven" on the back.
translations.idiomatic: Under Daming his income was lavish yet he still ran short; he bought on credit from townsfolk and, when pressed for payment, scrawled "forgiven" on the IOU.

sentences.zh: 善騎馬，解音律，遊行或三五百里，世祖恣其所之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at riding horses and understood music and pitch; on excursions he sometimes went three or five hundred li—Xiaowu let him go where he would.
translations.idiomatic: He rode well and knew music; his outings might run three to five hundred li—Xiaowu let him roam freely.

sentences.zh: 東至吳郡，登虎丘山，又登無錫縣烏山以望太湖。

translations.literal: East to Wu commandery he ascended Tiger Hill, and also ascended Wushan in Wuxi county to gaze on Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He went east to Wu, climbed Tiger Hill, then Mount Wu in Wuxi to view Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 大明中撰國史，世祖自為義恭作傳。

translations.literal: In Daming he compiled the national history; Xiaowu himself wrote Yigong's biography for it.
translations.idiomatic: During Daming he worked on the national history; Xiaowu personally wrote Yigong's biography for it.

sentences.zh: 及永光中，雖任宰輔，而承事近臣戴法興等，常若不及。

translations.literal: By the Yongguang era, though he held chief minister posts, toward close ministers like Dai Fazxing he often seemed unable to keep up.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongguang, though nominally chief minister, he deferred to close favorites such as Dai Fazxing as if he could never catch up.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝狂悖無道，義恭、元景等謀欲廢立。

translations.literal: Former Deposed Emperor was mad and without the Way; Yigong, Yuan Jing, and others plotted to depose and install.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor was violently lawless; Yigong, Yuan Jing, and others plotted to replace him.

sentences.zh: 永光元年八月，廢帝率羽林兵於第害之，並其四子，時年五十三。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongguang the Deposed Emperor led feathered guard soldiers to his residence and killed him together with his four sons; he was fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongguang year one, eighth month, the Deposed Emperor sent palace guards to Yigong's house and killed him with his four sons; he was fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 斷析義恭支體，分裂腸胃，挑取眼精，以蜜漬之，以為鬼目粽。

translations.literal: They severed and dissected Yigong's limbs, split belly and intestines, picked out the eyeballs, pickled them in honey, and made them into "ghost-eye zongzi."
translations.idiomatic: They hacked apart Yigong's body, split open his belly, scooped out his eyes, pickled them in honey, and called the result "ghost-eye dumplings."

sentences.zh: 太宗定亂，令書曰：「故中書監、太宰、領太尉、錄尚書事江夏王道性淵深，睿鑒通遠，樹聲列藩，宣風鉉德，位隆姬輔，任屬負圖，勤勞國家，方熙託付之重，盡心毗導，永融雍穆之化。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming settled the chaos he issued a letter, saying: "The late Director of the Palace Secretariat, Grand Preceptor, concurrent Grand Commandant, Recorder of Master of Writing affairs, Prince of Jiangxia—his Way-nature was deep, his wise mirror penetrating and far; he raised fame among the feudal ranks and proclaimed virtue at the imperial hinge; rank lofty as Ji aide, charge bearing the diagram; he toiled for the state and was just flourishing with the weight of entrustment, exhausting heart in assisting and guiding, forever blending harmonious and reverent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming restored order he wrote: "The late Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, Director of the Secretariat, Grand Preceptor, Grand Commandant, and chief of the Masters of Writing—his character ran deep, his judgment far-seeing; he won renown in the provinces and spread virtue at court; as chief kin he bore the burden of empire and labored for the state, guiding the realm toward harmony.

sentences.zh: 而凶醜忌威，奄加冤害，夷戮有暴，殯穸無聞，憤達幽明，痛貫朝野。

translations.literal: Yet the fierce villain hated his authority and suddenly added wrongful harm; slaughter was violent, burial mound unheard of—indignation reached yin and yang, pain pierced court and realm.
translations.idiomatic: The tyrant hated his stature and murdered him unjustly; the slaughter was savage and he received no proper burial—outrage reached heaven and earth, grief pierced the court.

sentences.zh: 朕蒙險在難，含哀莫申，幸賴宗祏之靈，克纂祈天之祚，仰惟勳戚，震慟於厥心。

translations.literal: I received peril in hardship, containing grief unable to express; fortunate to rely on the ancestral temple's spirit, able to succeed to the prayer-for-Heaven throne; looking up at meritorious kin, shock and grief in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I endured peril and could not mourn as I wished; by the ancestral spirits' grace I took the throne; thinking of my kinsman's merit, my heart shudders with grief.

sentences.zh: 昔梁王征庸，警蹕備禮；

translations.literal: In olden times the Liang king was summoned for service—warning clearances and full ceremony;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the King of Liang was summoned to serve—the throne cleared his path with full ceremony;

sentences.zh: 東平好善，黃屋在廷。

translations.literal: the Prince of Dongping loved goodness—the yellow canopy was in the court.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Dongping loved virtue—the imperial canopy attended him in court.

sentences.zh: 況公德猷弘懋，彝典未殊者哉！

translations.literal: How much more when your virtue and plan are grand and flourishing—the canonical rites are not different!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when your virtue and design are vast—should the canonical honors differ!

sentences.zh: 可追崇使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、丞相、領太尉，中書監、錄尚書事、王如故。

translations.literal: He may posthumously be honored Bearer of the Credential Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander over all military affairs inside and outside, Chancellor, concurrent Grand Commandant, Director of the Palace Secretariat, Recorder of Master of Writing affairs, Prince unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously honored as Bearer of the Credential Staff, Palace Attendant, commander of all armies within and without, Chancellor and Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat and chief of the Masters of Writing, with princely rank restored.

sentences.zh: 給九旒鸞輅，虎賁班劍百人，前後部羽葆、鼓吹，轀輬車。」

translations.literal: Granted nine tassels and the imperial phoenix carriage, a hundred tiger-guard ceremonial guards with drawn swords, front and rear feather canopies and ceremonial drums and horns, and the imperial mourning carriage."
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the nine-tassel phoenix carriage, a hundred tiger guards with ritual swords, front and rear feather canopies with drums and horns, and the imperial mourning coach."

sentences.zh: 泰始三年，又下詔曰：「皇基崇建，《屯》、《剝》維難，弘啟熙載，底績忠果，故從饗世祀，勒勳宗彝。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi another edict said: "The imperial foundation is loftily built—Difficulty and Splitting were the trials; broadly opening glorious burden, achieving merit through loyal fruit—therefore they follow in sacrifice through the ages, their achievements carved in the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year three another edict read: "The throne was raised amid hardship like the Hexagrams Difficulty and Splitting; loyal service built its glory—so they share in sacrificial honor through the ages, their deeds engraved in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 世祖寧亂定業，實資翼亮。

translations.literal: Xiaowu settled chaos and fixed the enterprise—truly relying on assistive brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu quelled rebellion and secured the realm with their steadfast support.

sentences.zh: 故使持節、侍中、都督中外諸軍事、丞相、領太尉、中書監、錄尚書事江夏文獻王義恭，故使持節、侍中、都督南豫、江、豫三州軍事、太尉、南豫州刺史、巴東郡開國忠烈公元景，故侍中、司空、始興郡開國襄公慶之，故持節、征西將軍、雍州刺史、洮陽縣開國肅侯愨，或體道沖玄，燮化康世，或盡誠致效，庚難龕逆，宜式遵國典，陪祭廟庭。」

translations.literal: Therefore Bearer of the Credential Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander over all military affairs inside and outside, Chancellor, concurrent Grand Commandant, Director of the Palace Secretariat, Recorder of Master of Writing affairs Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia Yigong; Bearer of the Credential Staff, Palace Attendant, Commander over the military affairs of Southern Yu, Jiang, and Yu provinces, Grand Commandant, Governor of Southern Yu, Duke of Badong commandery with open state, Loyal and Fierce Yuan Jing; Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, Duke of Shixing commandery with open state, Xiang Gong Qingzhi; Bearer of the Credential Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, Governor of Yongzhou, Marquis Su of Taoyang county with open state Min—some embodied the Way in serene mystery and harmonized transformation to bring peace to the age; some exhausted loyalty and showed effect, bearing difficulty and suppressing rebellion—they should follow the state canon and accompany sacrifice in the temple court."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuxian of Jiangxia Yigong, Bearer of the Credential Staff, Chancellor, Grand Commandant, Director of the Secretariat and chief of the Masters of Writing; Yuan Jing, Loyal and Fierce Duke of Badong, Grand Commandant and Governor of Southern Yu; Xiang Gong Qingzhi, Minister of Works and Duke of Shixing; and Marquis Su Min of Taoyang, General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yong—some harmonized the age through the Way, others gave loyal service in crushing rebellion—let them share temple sacrifice by state rite."

sentences.zh: 叡弟韶，字元和，封新吳縣侯，官至步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Rui's younger brother Shao, courtesy name Yuanhe, was enfeoffed Marquis of Xinwu county and reached the post of Commandant of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's brother Shao, styled Yuanhe, was made Marquis of Xinwu and rose to Commandant of Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 追贈中書侍郎，諡曰烈侯。

translations.literal: Posthumously promoted to Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat; posthumous title Liehou, Fierce Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Gentleman of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Fierce Marquis.

sentences.zh: 韶弟坦，字元度，平都懷侯。

translations.literal: Shao's younger brother Tan, courtesy name Yuandu, was Marquis Huai of Pingdu.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's brother Tan, styled Yuandu, was Marquis Huai of Pingdu.

sentences.zh: 坦弟元諒，江安愍侯。

translations.literal: Tan's younger brother Yuanliang was Marquis Min of Jiangan.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's brother Yuanliang was Marquis Min of Jiangan.

sentences.zh: 元諒弟元粹，興平悼侯。

translations.literal: Yuanliang's younger brother Yuancui was Marquis Dao of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanliang's brother Yuancui was Marquis Dao of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 坦、元諒、元粹並追贈散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Tan, Yuanliang, and Yuancui were all posthumously promoted to Gentleman of the Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, Yuanliang, and Yuancui were all posthumously made Gentlemen of the Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 元粹弟元仁、元方、元旒、元淑、元胤與朗等凡十二人，竝為元兇所殺。

translations.literal: Yuancui's younger brothers Yuanren, Yuanfang, Yuanliu, Yuanshu, and Yuanyin together with Lang and others—twelve in all—were all killed by the arch-criminal.
translations.idiomatic: Yuancui's brothers Yuanren, Yuanfang, Yuanliu, Yuanshu, and Yuanyin, with Lang and others—twelve in all—were all slain by the usurper.

sentences.zh: 元胤弟伯禽，孝建三年生。

translations.literal: Yuanyin's younger brother Boqin was born in the third year of Xiaojian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyin's brother Boqin was born in Xiaojian year three.

sentences.zh: 義恭諸子既遇害，為朝廷所哀，至是世祖名之曰伯禽，以擬魯公伯禽，周公旦之子也。

translations.literal: After Yigong's sons suffered harm the court mourned them; at this time Xiaowu named him Boqin, comparing him to Duke Boqin of Lu, son of the Duke of Zhou, Dan.
translations.idiomatic: When Yigong's sons were murdered the court grieved; Xiaowu named this child Boqin, evoking Duke Boqin of Lu, son of the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 官至輔國將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: He reached the post of General Who Supports the State and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to General Who Supports the State and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又為前廢帝所殺。

translations.literal: He was again killed by Former Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Deposed Emperor killed him as well.

sentences.zh: 諡曰哀世子。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Lamented Heir.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Lamented Heir.

sentences.zh: 又追贈江夏王，改諡曰愍。

translations.literal: He was also posthumously promoted to Prince of Jiangxia; the posthumous title was changed to Min.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Prince of Jiangxia with the altered posthumous title Min.

sentences.zh: 伯禽弟仲容，封永修縣侯。

translations.literal: Boqin's younger brother Zhongrong was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongxiu county.
translations.idiomatic: Boqin's brother Zhongrong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongxiu.

sentences.zh: 為寧朔將軍、臨淮、濟陽二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was General of Pacification and Grand Administrator of Linhuai and Jiyang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General of Pacification and governor of Linhuai and Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 仲容弟叔子，封永陽縣侯。

translations.literal: Zhongrong's younger brother Shuzi was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong's brother Shuzi was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 叔子弟叔寶，及仲容、叔子，竝為前廢帝所殺。

translations.literal: Shuzi's younger brother Shubao, together with Zhongrong and Shuzi, were all killed by Former Deposed Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzi's brother Shubao, with Zhongrong and Shuzi, were all killed by the Former Deposed Emperor.

sentences.zh: 諡仲容、叔子竝曰殤侯。

translations.literal: Posthumous titles for Zhongrong and Shuzi were both Shanghou, Marquis Who Died Young.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong and Shuzi both received the posthumous title Marquis Who Died Young.

sentences.zh: 義季素嗜酒，自彭城王義康廢後，遂為長夜之飲，略少醒日。

translations.literal: Yiji by nature loved wine; after Prince of Pengcheng Yikang was deposed, he then drank through the long night, scarcely waking by day.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji was devoted to wine; after Prince Yikang of Pengcheng was deposed he drank through the night and barely saw daylight.

sentences.zh: 太祖累加詰責，義季引愆陳謝。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen repeatedly added rebuke and censure; Yiji cited fault and submitted apology.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu rebuked him again and again; Yiji apologized and confessed fault.

sentences.zh: 上詔報之曰：「誰能無過，改之為貴耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor's edict in reply said: "Who can be without fault? To reform is precious.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: "Who is without fault? What matters is to reform.

sentences.zh: 此非唯傷事業，亦自損性命，世中比比，皆汝所諳。

translations.literal: This not only harms your enterprise but also damages your life itself—through the world such cases abound, all familiar to you.
translations.idiomatic: It harms not only your career but your very life—examples fill the world, and you know them well.

sentences.zh: 近長沙兄弟，皆緣此致故。

translations.literal: Recently the brothers of Changsha all met their end because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Not long ago the sons of Changsha all died for this very reason.

sentences.zh: 將軍蘇徽，耽酒成疾，旦夕待盡，吾試禁斷，並給藥膳，至今能立。

translations.literal: General Su Hui, indulging in wine until ill, awaited death morning and night; I tried forbidding and cutting off and also supplied medicine and diet—until now he can stand.
translations.idiomatic: General Su Hui drank himself sick and was near death; I forbade his wine and gave him medicine and food—he stands alive today.

sentences.zh: 此自是可節之物，但嗜者不能立志裁割耳。

translations.literal: This itself is a thing that can be measured; only those addicted cannot set will and cut it off.
translations.idiomatic: Wine can be rationed; only the addicted cannot resolve to cut it off.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝人主，尚能感王導之諫，終身不復飲酒。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Jin as ruler still could be moved by Wang Dao's remonstrance and for life never again drank wine.
translations.idiomatic: Even Emperor Yuan of Jin, though a sovereign, heeded Wang Dao's remonstrance and never drank again.

sentences.zh: 汝既有美尚，加以吾意殷勤，何至不能慨然深自勉厲，乃復須嚴相割裁，坐諸紜紜，然後少止者。

translations.literal: You already have fine aspirations, and moreover my intent is earnest—how could you not sigh deeply and strongly urge yourself, yet still need stern cutting and restraint, sitting among the crowd, and only then slightly stop?
translations.idiomatic: You have noble inclinations and my concern is earnest—why must you wait for harsh restraint among the court before you slightly relent?

sentences.zh: 幸可不至此，一門無此酣法，汝於何得之？

translations.literal: Fortune may not reach this point—no one in the house has this drunken way; from where did you obtain it?
translations.idiomatic: I hope it need not come to that—no one in our house drinks like this; where did you learn it?

sentences.zh: 臨書歎塞。」

translations.literal: Writing this letter I sigh and choke."
translations.idiomatic: I write this with sighs and sorrow."

sentences.zh: 義季雖奉此旨，酣縱如初，遂以成疾。

translations.literal: Yiji though received this intent, drank wildly as before and thus fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji received the edict yet drank as wildly as before and fell ill.

sentences.zh: 上又詔之曰：「汝飲積食少，而素羸多風，常慮至此，今果委頓。

translations.literal: The Emperor again issued an edict to him: "You drink much and eat little, and by nature are thin with much wind— I often feared reaching this; now indeed you are prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wrote again: "You drink heavily and eat little; you were always thin and prone to chills—I feared this day, and now you are collapsed.

sentences.zh: 縱不能以家國為懷，近不復顧性命之重，可歎可恨，豈復一條。

translations.literal: Even if you cannot take house and state to heart, recently you no longer regard the weight of life—lamentable and hateful, not just one matter.
translations.idiomatic: Even if you care nothing for realm or family, you no longer value your own life—wretched and infuriating, in more ways than one.

sentences.zh: 本望能以理自厲，未欲相苦耳。

translations.literal: I originally hoped you could urge yourself by reason and did not wish to distress you.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped you would discipline yourself by reason and did not mean to torment you.

sentences.zh: 今遣孫道胤就楊佛等令晨夕視汝，並進止湯食，可開懷虛受，慎勿隱避。

translations.literal: Now I send Sun Daoyin to Yang Fo and others to have them watch you morning and evening and also advance stopping soup and food—you may open your heart and empty receive; carefully do not hide and avoid.
translations.idiomatic: I send Sun Daoyin to Yang Fo and others to watch you day and night and regulate your meals—accept their care openly; do not evade them.

sentences.zh: 吾飽嘗見人斷酒，無它慊吸，蓋是當時甘嗜罔己之意耳。

translations.literal: I have fully seen people cut off wine—no other regret or craving; it is merely the sweet addiction at the time deceiving oneself.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen men quit wine—they suffer no other craving; it is only the sweetness of the habit fooling oneself.

sentences.zh: 今者憂怛，政在性命，未暇及美業，復何為吾煎毒至此邪！」

translations.literal: Now worry and grief—the government is life itself; no leisure for fine enterprise—why again do you torment me to this point!"
translations.idiomatic: Now my worry is for your life, not your career—why do you torture me so!"

sentences.zh: 義季終不改，以至於終。

translations.literal: Yiji to the end did not reform, until his death.
translations.idiomatic: Yiji never changed and drank until he died.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，為都督南兗、徐、青、冀、幽六州諸軍事、征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、南兗州刺史，持節、常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was made Commander over the military affairs of Southern Yan, Xu, Qing, Ji, and You provinces, General Who Pacifies the North and Grand General, Grand Master with ceremonial privileges as the Three Excellencies, Governor of Southern Yan, with credential staff and Regular Attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one he became commander of Southern Yan, Xu, Qing, Ji, and You, General Who Pacifies the North and Grand General with Three Excellencies ceremony, Governor of Southern Yan, keeping his commission and regular attendance.

sentences.zh: 登舟之日，帷帳器服，諸應隨刺史者，悉留之，荊楚以為美談。

translations.literal: On the day he boarded the boat, curtains, tents, vessels, and dress—all that should follow the governor—he left them all behind; Jing and Chu took this as a fine tale.
translations.idiomatic: When he embarked he left behind every curtain, vessel, and insignia due a governor—Jing and Chu praised the story.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，進督豫州之梁郡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was advanced to command Liang commandery of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two he gained command over Liang commandery in Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷徐州刺史，持節、常侍、都督如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Xuzhou; credential staff, Regular Attendant, and command unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Governor of Xuzhou with commission, attendance, and command unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明年，索虜侵逼，北境擾動，義季懲義康禍難，不欲以功勤自業，無它經略，唯飲酒而已。

translations.literal: The next year the Northern Wei pressed and invaded; the northern border was disturbed; Yiji took warning from Yikang's disaster and hardship and did not wish to make merit and diligence his enterprise—no other strategy, only drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Next year the Wei invaders pressed the border; mindful of Yikang's fate, Yiji refused to seek glory in arms and did nothing but drink.

sentences.zh: 太祖又詔之曰：「杜驥、申怙，倉卒之際，尚以弱甲瑣卒，徼寇作援。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen again issued an edict to him: "Du Ji and Shen Gu, in hurried crisis, still with weak armor and petty troops sought the bandits and made support.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu wrote again: "Du Ji and Shen Gu, in sudden crisis, still rallied meager troops to harry the enemy.

sentences.zh: 彼為元統，士馬桓桓，既不懷奮發，連被意旨，猶復逡巡。

translations.literal: You hold the primary banner, soldiers and horses imposing—yet neither cherish stirring to action nor, though repeatedly receiving intent, still hesitate.
translations.idiomatic: You command the main force with strong armies—yet you neither rouse yourself nor, despite repeated orders, stir.

sentences.zh: 豈唯大乖應赴之宜，實孤百姓之望。

translations.literal: Not only greatly contrary to the fitness of responding—truly betraying the people's hope.
translations.idiomatic: This not only betrays military duty but abandons the people's hope.

sentences.zh: 且匈奴輕漢，將自此而始。

translations.literal: Moreover the Xiongnu will lightly regard Han—starting from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this the barbarians will learn to despise Han.

sentences.zh: 賊初起逸，未知指趨，故且裝束，兼存觀察耳。

translations.literal: The bandits at first fled loosely, their aim unknown—therefore for the moment outfitting, also keeping observation.
translations.idiomatic: At first the enemy roamed loosely and their aim was unclear—you were merely to prepare and watch.

sentences.zh: 少日勢漸可見，便應大有經略，何合安然，遂不敢動。

translations.literal: In a few days the trend gradually could be seen—then there should have been great strategy; why fittingly sit at peace and then not dare move?
translations.idiomatic: Within days their course would show itself—you should have acted boldly; why sit idle and dare not move?

sentences.zh: 遣軍政欲乘際會，拯危急，以申威援，本無驅馳平原，方幅爭鋒理。

translations.literal: Sending the army the government wished to seize the occasion, rescue urgent peril, and declare authority and aid—originally not driving across the plain in square formation contending edge.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent troops to seize the moment, relieve crisis, and show imperial might—not to chase them across open plains in pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 又山路易憑，何以畏首尾迥弱。

translations.literal: Moreover mountain roads are easy to rely on—why fear head and tail, distant weakness?
translations.idiomatic: Mountain paths favor defense—why shrink before them at both ends?

sentences.zh: 若謂事理政應如此者，進大鎮，聚甲兵，徒為煩耳。」

translations.literal: If you say affairs and principle truly should be thus—advancing the great garrison, gathering armor and troops—is merely trouble."
translations.idiomatic: If you think this is how things should be—massing troops at the great garrison is only wasted effort."

sentences.zh: 二十四年，義季病篤，上遣中書令徐湛之省疾，召還京師。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Yiji's illness was grave; the Emperor sent Director of the Palace Secretariat Xu Zhizhi to visit the sickness and summon him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four Yiji lay gravely ill; Taizu sent Secretariat Director Xu Zhizhi to see him and recall him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 未及發，薨於彭城，時年三十三。

translations.literal: Before he could depart he died at Pengcheng; he was thirty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave he died at Pengcheng, aged thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 太尉江夏王義恭表解職迎喪，不許。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Prince of Jiangxia Yigong memorialized to resign office and meet the bier—not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Prince Yigong of Jiangxia asked to resign and meet the funeral procession—the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 上遣東海王禕北迎義季喪。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Prince Yi of Donghai north to meet Yiji's bier.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent Prince Yi of Donghai north to receive Yiji's coffin.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、司空，持節、都督、刺史如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously promoted Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; credential staff, command, and governorship unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works with commission, command, and governorship unchanged.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：戒懼乎其所不睹，恐畏乎其所不聞，在於慎所忽也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Be vigilant in what one does not see, fear what one does not hear—the point lies in being careful of what is neglected.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Be wary of what you cannot see and fear what you cannot hear—true caution lies in what is overlooked.

sentences.zh: 江夏王，高祖寵子，位居上相，大明之世，親典冠朝。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangxia was Gaozu's favored son, place at chief minister, in the Daming era personally presiding at the head of court.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yigong of Jiangxia was Gaozu's beloved son, a chief minister who in the Daming era stood at the head of court.

sentences.zh: 屈體降情，盤辟於軒檻之上，明其為卑約亦已至矣。

translations.literal: Bending body and lowering feeling, bowing and sidestepping on the hall's threshold—making clear his humility and restraint had already reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed low on the palace steps—his humility had already gone to the extreme.

sentences.zh: 得使虐朝暴主，顧無猜色，歷載逾十，以尊戚自保。

translations.literal: He could make tyrannical court and violent ruler look back without suspicious color; over more than ten years by honored kinship he preserved himself.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he endured tyrannical emperors without rousing suspicion, preserving himself through kinship and rank.

sentences.zh: 及在永光，幼主南面，公旦之重，屬有所歸。

translations.literal: When in Yongguang the young lord faced south, the weight of the Duke of Zhou had its place to return.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongguang, when a child sat the throne, the burden of a Duke of Zhou seemed at last to have found its home.

sentences.zh: 自謂踐冰之慮已除，泰山之安可恃，曾未云幾，而磔體分肌。

translations.literal: He himself thought the worry of treading ice was removed, Mount Tai's peace could be relied on—scarcely had it been said when body was torn and flesh divided.
translations.idiomatic: He thought the peril of walking on ice was past and Mount Tai's stability assured—yet almost at once his body was hacked apart.

sentences.zh: 古人以隱微致戒，斯為篤矣。

translations.literal: The ancients by hidden and subtle gave warning—this is profound indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients warned through what is hidden and slight—how deep that lesson runs.
